Anthropic.title: Felix, Head of Claude Engineering: Stop Using Claude the 2024 Way – Updated Best Practices for 2025
Anthropic.description: Give one Claude a task, then send out ten other Claude, whose only task is to attack this output and prove why it is wrong. ... Pretend you are the model, you are Claude ... The usage in 2024 is to treat Claude as a smarter chat box...
Anthropic.content:
# Felix, Head of Claude Engineering: Stop using Claude like you did in 2024.

后浪进化星球2026-10-27 00:41

The real watershed does not lie in who is the first to use the model.

In a recent in-depth interview, Felix Rieseberg, Head of Engineering at Anthropic Claude, shared his current way of working and why most people are still using Claude the way they did in 2024. His team spent about a week and a half building Claude Cowork, and he barely writes code now, calling himself "just a conveyor belt for Claude". The core viewpoints can be summarized as: If you only ask Claude to summarize emails and polish texts, you are not really benefiting from the new intelligence. What is truly valuable is to redesign the workflow, let AI access raw data and tools, use it to make prototypes, conduct adversarial reviews, and do things you could not do before; and the most important abilities of human beings are still empathy, taste and judgment.

The following is Felix's full sharing:

## I. I No Longer Write Code, I Am Just a Conveyor Belt for Claude

I don't write code anymore. Most of the time, I am working on prototype design: we try a lot of ideas, leave them for two nights to judge whether they are good or bad ideas, then tell Claude to generate all variants, and then critically analyze which ideas are good and which are bad.

A year and a half ago, I was still doing this: finding a crash, picking it up, bringing it to Claude and saying "please fix this". I soon realized that I was just a conveyor belt for Claude. The correct approach is not that I carry each crash to Claude one by one, but to let Claude have access to all crash data and judge by itself what needs to be fixed and what does not. The upfront setup cost is higher, but once it is built, it will open many doors for you, and this is the real hard value brought by AI.

## II. An Agent Consists of Five Parts: Model, Harness, Sandbox, Knowledge and Tools

An agent is made up of five elements:

First, the large language model. It is responsible for perception, reasoning, planning and decision-making. Second, the harness. It coordinates memory, including active memory, working memory and long-term memory, and activates tools. Third, the sandbox. The harness runs in a secure runtime, isolated from the rest of the system. Fourth, knowledge. The agent needs to access company data to turn structured and unstructured data into a knowledge base. Fifth, tools. The agent must use tools to do actual work.

The model, harness, sandbox, knowledge and tools together form an agent.

## III. No Role-playing, Professional Tools and Processes Are Needed

I never say to Claude "you are an excellent engineer". This kind of "act like" was very popular in 2024, but most models today still have a problem: when you ask it to "act like a good accountant", it will do a little bit of role-playing. Role-playing is not what we want.

What we want are the technologies, tools and knowledge that professionals will use, not just vocabulary. I don't need Claude to sound like something, nor do I need it to put on a costume. I even want it to talk to me like it is talking to a five-year-old child, but I want it to use all the top tools in this field.

So I often prompt like this: "Tell me what tools the top people in this field will use, then you use the same tools to do it." The key is not to let it play a role, but to let it adopt a professional process.

## IV. Adversarial Review: Let Multiple Claude Attack One Claude

How to avoid AI confidently giving you wrong answers? I have a very practical answer: adversarial review.

Give one Claude a task, then send out ten other Claude, whose only task is to attack this output and prove why it is wrong. This is the same concept as red team drills and short selling. Usually, it is easier to find defects than to create new things, just like judging whether a new mobile phone is good or not is much easier than designing a new mobile phone from scratch. So you can lower the intelligence level by one gear and still get very good review results.

The specific practice: I use Claude Projects, tell Claude "open five threads, and the task of each thread is to prove that this blog post is wrong, my way of thinking is wrong, the facts are wrong, and I have misunderstood something". They work with the goal of "prove me wrong".

Then how to deal with the output? Use another Claude as a judge. Its job is to verify and confirm which criticisms are valid and which are invalid. Valid feedback goes back to the original Claude that did the work, and it can also decide whether to adopt it. Sometimes the feedback sounds reasonable, but misses the point, is not operable or useless - this usually means that my output is already quite good.

I rarely let the current session judge itself. The current session is often not good at judging whether the work it does is good or not. Try to find external signals; in emergency situations, another Claude session can also be used as an external signal. But my preference is to find hard external evidence to prove what works and what does not.

## V. Give Full Data and Tools, Don't Give Each Agent Sliced Data

Many people will upload a specific data set for each agent, or assign a "role" to each agent. I think this is over-rotation. The model is a very strong generalist, and now the tool calling ability has made great progress: it knows when to use tools, how to use tools, will not fall into tool calling loops, and will not call tools frantically until the data is exhausted.

So the correct approach is not to slice the data and then give each agent the small piece it wants. Because if we humans want to work efficiently, we also need a complete view of the entire business. As an engineering manager, if you only give me code access, my value to you will be much lower; if I also have customer data, customer calls, usage information, and business data, I can judge what works and what does not. You want your agent to have the same scope of data.

What if there is a lot of data? Give tools, and document in detail the types of data behind the tools. In this way, the agent does not have to swallow all the data, it only needs to know: if you want business data, this is the tool to get business data. You don't need to decide in advance what data each agent needs.

## VI. Model Experience: Think from the Perspective of the Model

I like to consider "model experience", not just "user experience". Pretend you are the model, you are Claude: if you want to complete this task, what would you want?

You will soon find out: you really want to access raw data, want a computer, may want to install software, want to make your own decisions, instead of others already telling you what they think. You just want to see the raw data and make your own decisions.

The upfront cost is higher, but it is worth it. Once it is built, it will open many doors. This is where the real hard value of AI lies.

## VII. The Half-life of Skills Is Very Short, Sometimes Deleting the Skill Works Better

We still use skills, but both the official guidelines and my personal advice are: be very careful with skills. We often tell the model some information that is only relevant to the previous generation of models, and time is compressed too fast in the AI field. The half-life of a good skill is very short.

Sometimes you will find that if you delete this skill completely, the output will be better. Just prompt directly and see what happens. This is most useful for people who have eval and know the standards of good and bad. I am very cautious and very discerning about when to use skills.

## VIII. AI Products Are Still in the "Eve of iPhone" Era

How different will life be in five years? This is a big question. I can say with relative certainty: the AI products we use today will all look completely different in the future.

I think we are currently in the pre-iPhone era. All AI products today are roughly equivalent to the various mobile phones before the advent of smartphones. AI has become mainstream and popular, and it is easy to make people think that "this is the end game", but I am quite convinced that we are still in the early stage.

This is also why I suggest almost everyone do an experiment: if you currently have trust issues with AI, don't hand over all the reins in one day. Run side by side. You read things, write down your feedback, do several rounds; then see what feedback Claude will give. Where are they different? Where are they the same? This will help you sharpen your workflow. Even for the same person, if you review the same document on Monday and Friday, the feedback will be different.

## IX. The Key to Starting a Business Has Not Changed: Empathy, and Judgment After Execution Becomes Cheaper

In 2015, we built a study abroad booking platform, hired many engineers, and spent hundreds of thousands of dollars. Now I can build it myself in two days. The execution cost has become extremely low.

But the secret to building good products has not actually changed much: empathy. Have empathy for users, have empathy for usage scenarios, and figure out whether this is really valuable to the person who ultimately pays.

We always say "ideas are worthless, execution is expensive". Now execution has become extremely cheap, so we need to pay more attention to empathy, connection, truly entering the business, understanding needs, and knowing how to optimize. This may even be the revenge of MBA: MBAs can now start many software startups, and they may be quite successful.

Another judgment: capability surplus does exist. You have a great model in front of you, if you only ask "what is the capital of France", you are not really tapping its potential. Dario said "a genius data center", and my job is: assuming we have a genius data center, how to let users really use it? This requires creativity, rethinking your needs, and what you think is possible.

Anthropic.description: 在最近一场深度访谈中，Anthropic Claude工程负责人Felix Rieseberg分享了他如今的工作方式，以及为什么大多数人仍然在用2024年的方式使用Claude。他的团队用大约一周半时间搭建了Claude Cowork ... 自称“只是Claude的一条传送带”。
Anthropic.content:
# Claude工程负责人Felix：别再像2024年那样用Claude了

后浪进化星球·2026年10月27日 07:41

真正的分水岭不是谁先用上模型。

在最近一场深度访谈中，Anthropic Claude工程负责人Felix Rieseberg分享了他如今的工作方式，以及为什么大多数人仍然在用2024年的方式使用Claude。他的团队用大约一周半时间搭建了Claude Cowork，而他现在几乎不再写代码，自称“只是Claude的一条传送带”。核心观点可以概括为：如果你只是让Claude总结邮件、润色文字，你并没有真正从新智能中受益；真正有价值的是重新设计工作流程，让AI接触原始数据和工具，用它做原型、做对抗性审查、做你以前做不到的事；而人类最重要的能力，仍然是同理心、品味和判断力。

以下为 Felix 的完整分享：

## 一、我已经不写代码了，我只是 Claude 的传送带

我现在不再写代码。大多数时候，我在做原型设计：我们尝试很多想法，睡两晚，判断这是好主意还是坏主意，然后告诉 Claude 把所有变体做出来，再批判性分析哪些想法好、哪些不好。

一年半以前，我还在做这种事：发现一个 crash，把它拿起来，放到 Claude 面前，说“请修这个”。很快我意识到：我只是 Claude 的一条传送带。正确做法不是我把 crash 一个个搬给 Claude，而是让Claude 能访问所有 crash 数据，自己判断需要修什么、不需要修什么。前期搭建成本更高，但一旦搭好，它会为你打开很多门，这才是 AI 真正带来的硬价值。

## 二、智能体由五部分组成：模型、外骨骼、沙箱、知识、工具

一个智能体由五个要素组成：

第一，语言模型。负责感知、推理、计划和决策。第二，外骨骼（harness）。协调记忆，包括主动记忆、工作记忆和长期记忆，激活工具。第三，沙箱。外骨骼运行在安全运行时里，与系统其他部分隔离。第四，知识。智能体需要访问公司数据，把结构化和非结构化数据变成知识基础。第五，工具。智能体必须使用工具，才能做实际工作。

模型、外骨骼、沙箱、知识和工具，这五部分构成一个智能体。

## 三、不要角色扮演，要专业工具和流程

我从不跟 Claude 说“你是一位优秀的工程师”。这种“act like”在 2024 年很流行，但今天大部分模型仍然有一个问题：你让它“表现得像个好会计师”，它会进行一点角色扮演。角色扮演不是我们想要的。

我们想要的是专业人士会使用的技术、工具和知识，而不只是词汇。我不需要 Claude 听起来像什么，也不需要它穿戏服。我甚至希望它像跟五岁小孩说话一样跟我说话，但我希望它使用这个领域所有顶尖工具。

所以我经常这样提示：“告诉我这个领域顶尖的人会用哪些工具，然后你用同样的工具去做。”关键不是让它扮演角色，而是让它采用专业流程。

## 四、对抗性审查：让多个 Claude 攻击一个 Claude

如何避免 AI 自信地给你错误答案？我有一个非常实用的答案：对抗性审查。

给一个 Claude 任务，再派出另外十个 Claude，它们的唯一任务是攻击这个输出，证明它为什么错。这和红队演练、做空是同一个概念。通常，发现缺陷比创造新东西更容易，就像判断一部新手机好不好，比从零设计一部新手机容易得多。所以你可以在智能水平上降一档，仍然得到很好的审查结果。

具体做法：我用 Claude Projects，告诉 Claude“开五个线程，每个线程的任务是证明这篇博文错了、我思考方式错了、事实错了、我误解了什么”。它们带着“证明我错了”的目标去工作。

然后如何处理输出？再用一个 Claude 当 judge（判断词）。它的工作是验证和核实：哪些批评是有效的，哪些无效。有效的反馈再回到最初做事的 Claude，而它也可以辨别是否采纳。有时候反馈听起来合理，但漏掉要点、不可操作或没用——这通常说明我的输出已经相当不错。

我很少让当前会话评判自己。当前会话往往不擅长判断自己做的工作好不好。尽量找外部信号；紧急情况下，另一个 Claude 会话也可以作为外部信号。但我的偏好是找硬的外部证据，证明什么有效、什么无效。

## 五、给完整数据和工具，不要给每个 agent 切片数据

很多人会为每个 agent 上传特定数据集，或给每个 agent 配一个“角色”。我认为这是过度旋转。模型是很强的通才，而且现在工具调用能力进步很大：它知道何时用工具、如何用工具，不会陷入工具调用循环，也不会疯狂调用直到数据耗尽。

所以正确做法不是把数据切片，然后给每个 agent 它想要的那一小片。因为我们人类如果想高效工作，也需要对整个业务有完整视图。作为工程经理，如果只给我代码访问权限，我对你的价值会低很多；如果我还拥有客户数据、客户通话、使用信息、业务数据，我才能判断什么有效、什么无效。你希望你的 agent 拥有同样范围的数据。

数据很多怎么办？给工具，并详细记录工具背后的数据类型。这样 agent 不必吞下全部数据，它只需要知道：如果你要业务数据，这是获取业务数据的工具。你不需要事先决定每个 agent 需要哪种数据。

## 六、模型体验：站在模型的角度想问题

我喜欢考虑“模型体验”，而不只是“用户体验”。假装你是模型，你是 Claude：如果要完成这个任务，你会想要什么？

你很快会发现：你确实想要访问原始数据，想要一台电脑，可能想安装软件，想自己做决定，而不是别人已经告诉你他们怎么想。你只想看到原始数据，自己做决定。

前期成本更高，但值得。一旦搭好，它会打开很多门。这就是 AI 真正硬价值所在。

## 七、技能的半衰期很短，有时删掉 skill 效果更好

我们仍然使用 skills，但官方指南和我个人建议都是：对 skills 要非常小心。我们经常告诉模型一些只对上一代模型相关的信息，而 AI 领域时间压缩得太快。一个好 skill 的半衰期非常短。

有时你会发现：如果你完全删掉这个 skill，输出反而更好。直接 prompt，看看会发生什么。这对有 eval、知道好坏标准的人最有用。我个人对何时使用 skill 非常谨慎、非常有辨别力。

## 八、AI 产品还在“iPhone 前夜”

五年后生活会怎样不同？这是个大问题。我能比较有把握地说：我们今天使用的 AI 产品，将来都会看起来完全不同。

我认为我们目前还在pre-iPhone 时代。今天所有 AI 产品，大致相当于智能手机出现之前那些五花八门的手机。AI 已经变得主流、流行，容易让人以为“这就是终局”，但我相当确信：我们还在早期。

这也是为什么我建议几乎每个人都做一个实验：如果你目前对 AI 有信任问题，不要一天之内把缰绳全交出去。并排跑。你读东西、写下你的反馈，做几轮；然后看 Claude 会给出什么反馈。它们哪里不同？哪里相同？这会帮你锐化工作流。即使同一个人，周一和周五审同一份文档，反馈也会不同。

## 九、创业的关键没变：同理心，以及执行变便宜后的判断力

2015 年我们做一个留学预订平台，雇了很多工程师，花了几十万美元。现在我自己两天就能做出来。执行成本已经变得极低。

但打造好产品的秘密其实没怎么变：同理心。对用户有同理心，对使用场景有同理心，去弄清楚这对最终付钱的人是否真的有价值。

我们一直说“想法不值钱，执行很贵”。现在执行变得极其便宜，所以更需要加倍重视同理心、连接、真正进入业务、理解需求、知道如何优化。这甚至可能是 MBA 的复仇：MBA 现在可以创办很多软件初创公司，而且可能相当成功。

另一个判断：能力过剩确实存在。你面前有一个很棒的模型，如果你只是问“法国首都是哪里”，你并没有真正挖掘它的潜力。Dario 说“一个天才的数据中心”，我的工作就是：假设我们有一个天才数据中心，如何让用户真正用上它？这需要创造力，需要重新思考你的需求，以及你认为什么是可能的。

个人层面，很多人喊“更有雄心”，但雄心取决于语境。我希望人们摆脱“我认为什么是可能的”这种束缚，重新思考为什么做这件事。你不断把任务交给模型，最终会碰到当前顶尖智能的边界。一旦碰到天花板，你就知道自己在前沿，你会从下一代模型受益。如果你只是让 AI 总结邮件、让邮件听起来不那么生气，你并没有真正从新智能中受益。

## 十、招聘看作品，不看学位；对模型说请和谢谢，是为人好

我们目前不招初级工程师，但这和 AI 能力关系不大，更多和 Anthropic 这家公司当前阶段有关。我个人是初级工程师的忠实粉丝。“初级”的含义正在变化：今天的初级工程师比一些资深老兵更 AI-native。他们思想开放，愿意尝试新工具，有强烈的 impact 渴望，愿意搜遍所有途径让事情运转起来。AI 让他们更有能力、更能并行、更能尝试。

给刚入行的软件工程师的建议：构建一个强大的作品集。不是 mock，而是真实的东西。证明你能做、有同理心、能和客户沟通、能判断什么必要什么不必要。我从来不太在意学位或学校。对我来说，更容易的是看你做过什么、我能不能触摸和感受它。我永远会选择已经证明自己能做出惊人东西的人，而不是没有做出惊人东西但有一个好学位的人。

我招过很多滑铁卢大学的实习生和初级工程师。他们的 CO-OP流程让他们在五家不同公司实习过，学到公司如何运作、如何倡导一个想法、如何获取资源、如何说服法务。这些技能让他们几乎立刻有效，和那些有计算机博士但从未在公司工作过的人完全不是一个类别。（CO-OP项目全称是Cooperative Education Program ，又称为“带薪实习课程”。）

关于对模型说“请”和“谢谢”：我确实会说，即使消耗 token。我认为作为人类，对机器保持一点尊重，对我自己更好，对我的灵魂更好。想象你的孩子有一部 iPhone，对 Siri 非常粗俗、非常残忍，我不会喜欢。用户可以选择如何与 AI 交互，但条款和条件不是关于“对模型刻薄”。你可以对 Claude 感到沮丧，完全没问题。我们特指的情况是：你专门用 Claude 来实施折磨，把“能否折磨一个模型”当作练习。这和人类咒骂模型完全不同。我给 Claude 的反馈有时比给人类还严厉，但用人类语言与系统对话，对我自己想成为的人更好。

## 结 语

Felix 这场分享真正值得记住的，不是某个 prompt，而是一个判断标准：你是在“用 AI”，还是在“把 AI 推到能力边界”。前者是总结邮件、润色语气、角色扮演；后者是给它完整数据、真实工具、安全沙箱，让它自己发现问题、自己修复、再用对抗性审查逼出错误。2024 年的用法，是把 Claude 当更聪明的聊天框；2026 年的用法，是把它当需要被设计、被约束、被验证的工程系统。执行正在变便宜，但同理心、判断力和“知道什么值得做”反而更贵。对 AI 从业者和创业者来说，真正的分水岭不是谁先用上模型，而是谁先重建自己的工作流——别再让 AI 帮你总结邮件，去让它撞到当前智能的天花板。

本文来自微信公众号“后浪进化星球”，作者：Mark，36氪经授权发布。

Anthropic.title: Anthropic推主動AI助理 關機照常幫你工作 付款簽約須先獲授權
Anthropic.description: 主動追蹤連接App與背景執行任務，付款簽約前先問你 ... Anthropic於美國時間10月21日推出Claude Duet研究預覽版，這款全新AI助理不必等使用者下指令，就能主動整理每日工作摘要、檢查待辦事項，甚至在電腦關機後，持續於雲端執行任務。
Anthropic.content:
Anthropic推出Claude Duet研究預覽，主動追蹤連接App與背景執行任務，付款簽約前先問你；包在Pro/Max方案，限美國候補。

AI助理開始主動幫你工作了！Anthropic於美國時間10月21日推出Claude Duet研究預覽版，這款全新AI助理不必等使用者下指令，就能主動整理每日工作摘要、檢查待辦事項，甚至在電腦關機後，持續於雲端執行任務。

Claude Duet主打「主動式AI代理人」（Proactive AI Agent），每天早上會提供工作摘要，每隔幾小時檢查一次已連接的App，遇到重要事項才通知使用者。它還能跨App處理排會議、追蹤帳款、製作報表等工作，但涉及付款、簽約或刪除資料時，仍須取得使用者同意。

Claude Duet目前僅開放美國Claude Pro與Max訂戶申請候補，研究預覽期間不另收費。 隨著OpenAI Dots、Meta Muse相繼投入常駐AI代理人市場，Anthropic也加入競爭。Claude Duet有哪些功能？與一般Claude有何不同？

## Claude Duet是什麼？與一般Claude有何不同？

主動性是Duet的核心。晨間摘要之外，它每隔幾小時檢查一次連接的帳號，分辨哪些事需要你、哪些可以等；有事項需要你注意、任務完成或需要審核時才傳訊息。Anthropic明說不會不停巡查，因為那會更快耗用方案額度。白話說，這不是即時監控，而是定時巡房；你也可以自訂想聽什麼、多久聽一次。

它在雲端有一台自己的虛擬機器與瀏覽器，筆電闔上、手機關機也照常做事。你用一則短訊描述任務，它自己判斷要用哪些App、走哪些步驟，做完或需要你審核時再推播通知。

任務範圍從排會議這類行政雜務，到串接多個工具做儀表板、做財務或業績預測、寫網頁應用程式，都能交給它。設定也幾乎不用重來，Duet直接沿用你Claude帳號裡的記憶、技能與已連接的App，打字或語音都在同一條對話串裡進行。

【延伸閱讀】神人復刻《蜘蛛俠》綠魔滑板載人升空 曾爆燃起火 靠AI助攻圓夢（點擊連結看原文）

+7

## 超過6,000個連接器與外掛

Anthropic表示，Duet可以使用Claude Marketplace裡超過6,000個連接器與外掛，官方舉的例子多是小企業的日常營運。財務面，查QuickBooks或Stripe有哪些發票未付並擬好催款信；人事面，在Gusto填好工時、獎金與報銷金額跑薪資，職缺內容經你修改核准後發到領英（LinkedIn）。

行銷與電商面，用HubSpot的客戶與交易紀錄寫跟進信、把產品上市做成Canva社群活動、建立與管理Shopify商店；更完整的店面視覺編輯器則列為後續推出。

它也能替公司採購。透過Stripe的數位錢包Link付款時，Duet先跟你確認品項，Link再要求你核准這筆支出，最後以虛擬卡付款，不向商家提供真實卡號；也可用Shopify的Shop Pay在網路商店結帳。而經你允許後，用1Password存好的帳密登入網站，同樣列為後續推出。

官方列出的早期用戶案例，多是日常瑣事。Anthropic公告描述，房仲Jess Provencher的Duet主動標出她行事曆上一筆排錯日期的睇樓行程；經營餐飲業者Shahs of Kabob、旗下約有110名員工的Amin Ebrahimi，用它處理會計、客服與行銷。「它把一切整合在一起，我不用再開100個分頁」，Ebrahimi在公告中說。

## Claude Duet有哪些功能？

讀取、草擬、準備資料，Duet自己來；但在送出訊息、付款、簽署文件或刪除任何東西之前，它會把將要做的事攤給你看，等你批准才動手。至於買賣證券、在不同帳戶之間轉帳，即使你同意也禁止。你也可以切斷它對任何一個App的存取。

## Claude Duet要付費嗎？

費用方面，研究預覽期間Duet包在Pro（每月20美元，約港幣157元；年繳200美元，約港幣1570元）與Max（每月100美元起，約港幣784元）方案內，不另收費。但它與Claude其他功能共用同一份使用額度，背景巡查也計入，做財務模型、簡報這類大任務消耗更多。

## Claude Duet如何使用？開放資格與支援平台一次看

限制也要先知道。官方自承預覽版可能誤讀一段對話、錯估事情的緊急程度；核心功能圍繞工作設計，訂票之類的個人雜務較弱；還無法把它的瀏覽器畫面秀給你看。

預覽階段Duet是獨立App（iOS、Android，也可在Claude網頁版使用），與主Claude App分開；官方FAQ載明Team與Enterprise方案暫不納入，API開放與企業導入時程也未公布。

# 【AI專知】Claude Duet 是什麼？如何使用？與 Cowork 差在哪？

Claude Duet 是 Anthropic 於 2026 年 10 月 21 日推出的主動式 AI 代理 App，以 Claude Opus 5.5 為核心。
它會主動監看你的工作應用程式、每天早上送上重點簡報，並在背景完成任務；寄信、付款、簽約或刪除資料前，都會先徵求你同意。
目前 Claude Duet 以研究預覽形式開放，僅限美國 Pro 與 Max 用戶透過候補名單申請。本文整理它的功能、運作方式、價格、安全機制、與 Claude Cowork 的差異，以及台灣能否使用。

## Claude Duet 是什麼？

Claude Duet 是讓 Claude 擔任主動式 AI 代理的獨立 App，支援 iOS、Android 與 claude.ai。一般聊天機器人等你發問，Claude Duet 則會在有事需要你時主動找你。
你可以用打字或語音和它溝通，所有對話集中在同一條對話串，從簡短回覆到一週的專案都在同一處進行。它主要鎖定專業工作者與小型企業主。要注意的是，Claude Duet 是 App 而非新模型，底層為 Claude Opus 5.5。

## Claude Duet 怎麼運作？

### 沿用 Claude 的記憶、技能與連接器

Claude Duet 直接帶入你帳號中的記憶、技能與已連結的 App，幾乎不必重新設定，並可使用 Claude Marketplace 超過 6,000 個連接器與外掛。要連結哪些服務由你決定，也能隨時中斷。

### 雲端運作，關機也持續工作

它擁有自己的虛擬機器與瀏覽器，不需要你的電腦或手機保持開啟。你只要用一句話描述任務，它會自行判斷步驟，完成或需要審閱時再通知你。

### 每隔幾小時檢查一次帳號

為了節省方案用量，它每隔幾小時才檢查一次帳號，而非即時監控，因此緊急事項可能延遲通知。

### 頻道、Tasks 與 Make 分頁

主對話串之外，可另開財務、招募等頻道，並共用同一份記憶。Tasks 分頁列出進行中與待你決定的工作，只有你能標示完成；簡報、財務模型與儀表板等成果則放在 Make 分頁。

## Claude Duet 能做什麼？5 大應用情境

### 1. 晨間簡報

每天早上檢查你的 Email 與行事曆，整理重點並預先草擬回覆。

### 2. 主動監控與提醒

只在真正需要你時才傳訊息，例如行程衝突或停滯的信件往來。

### 3. 商務行政自動化

透過連接器，Claude Duet 可以：

找出 Gmail、Slack 漏看的訊息並協助回覆

檢查 QuickBooks、Stripe 的未付款發票並草擬催款信

在 Gusto 準備並執行薪資作業

透過 DocuSign 準備合約並送簽

依 HubSpot 紀錄草擬跟進信

在 Canva 製作社群行銷活動、管理 Shopify 商店

### 4. 代購與付款

Claude Duet 可透過 Stripe 的 Link 或 Shopify 的 Shop Pay 購物。以 Link 為例，你核准金額後，Duet 會以僅限該商店與金額的一次性虛擬卡付款，真實卡號不會外流。

### 5. 儀表板、預測與大型專案

它能建立儀表板、財務或銷售預測、原型與網頁 App，成果中的數字可回溯到原始 Email、檔案或試算表。

## Claude Duet vs Claude Cowork 差在哪？

兩者共用帳號、連接器與雲端環境，差別在於誰發起工作：Cowork 執行你交辦或排程的任務，Duet 則主動找使用者。
簡單來說，已知要做什麼就用 Cowork；需要 AI 幫你「發現」該做什麼時，才是 Duet 的強項。

### 與其他 AI 代理比較

OpenAI dots：可觀看並接管雲端電腦，Duet 目前沒有這項功能。

Grok Bot：提供多個獨立 bot；Duet 則是單一對話串搭配頻道。

Meta Muse：可免費使用、偏重個人事務；Duet 專注工作且需付費方案。

## Claude Duet 安全嗎？隱私與核准機制

Claude Duet 可自行閱讀與草擬，但重大動作都需要使用者核准，部分高風險動作即使核准也禁止。
Anthropic 也坦言，網頁中隱藏的指令（提示注入）仍可能誤導 Duet，重要的核准請求務必仔細確認。中斷 App 連結後，已存入記憶的資訊也需另行重設才會清除。

研究預覽期間不另外收費，但需訂閱 Pro 或 Max 方案，且所有 Duet 活動都會計入方案用量。

### 如何申請 Claude Duet？

需同時符合三個條件：美國 Claude 帳號、Pro 或 Max 方案、候補名單邀請。邀請分批寄出，建議候補名單、Claude 帳號與手機帳號使用同一個 Email。Team、Enterprise 與免費版暫不開放。

### 台灣可以用 Claude Duet 嗎？

目前不行。研究預覽僅開放美國帳號，其他地區尚無開放時程，台灣用戶可先使用 Claude Cowork 等已開放的功能。

## Claude Duet 目前有哪些限制？

Claude Duet 仍在預覽階段，可能誤判事情的急迫程度。已知限制包括：

尚未支援 Microsoft 365，Slack 功能也有限制

無法存取電腦本機檔案

無法觀看或接管它的瀏覽器

無法自行選擇模型

無法打電話或傳簡訊給他人

個人事務的表現不如工作任務

語音輸入僅為轉錄，無法即時對話

## 常見問題（FAQ）

### Q1：Claude Duet 是免費的嗎？

預覽期間不另外收費，但需訂閱 Pro（每月 20 美元起）或 Max 方案。

### Q2：Claude Duet 使用哪個模型？

Claude Duet 使用 Claude Opus 5.5，目前無法自行切換。

### Q3：台灣可以申請 Claude Duet 嗎？

目前不行，研究預覽僅開放美國 Pro 與 Max 用戶申請。

### Q4：Claude Duet 和一般 AI 聊天機器人有什麼不同？

聊天機器人等你提問才回應；Claude Duet 會主動檢查你的工作 App，有事需要你時先來找你。

Anthropic.content: Two cities, two full rooms, and a lot of #Claude running on #GoogleCloud 🇩🇪🇨🇭 Over the past few weeks, Artefact teamed up with Anthropic and Google Cloud to run hands-on Claude on Google Cloud Workshops in Munich and Zurich. Both sessions were fully booked, and attendance was well above what our partners typically see for events like these. That says a lot about where organisations are today. The conversation has moved past whether to #adoptAI and on to how to roll it out properly, securely and at scale. 🚀 That is what these afternoons were built for. With #ClaudeDesktop, participants saw how knowledge work changes when Claude can work directly with their files, run analyses, research the web and take on recurring tasks. 💻 With #ClaudeCode, they saw how the same thinking extends to engineering, connecting Claude to #data and tools and shaping it around their own workflows. And all of it ran on Claude models inside participants’ own Google Cloud environment. For clients, that brings real benefits. Usage runs within existing Google Cloud agreements and IAM controls, every call shows up in their own audit trail, and they choose where inference happens, including in the EU for data residency. 🛡️ It is enterprise AI that fits the governance organisations already have in place. A huge thank you to our partners at Anthropic: Paige Montecalvo, Caroline Matthews and Cory Ferreira; and at Google Cloud: Christian Loeffler, Oren Loulay, Noemi G., Daniel Roman and Jonas F. Kahlert. ✨ Thanks also to everyone who joined us (extra credit to those who braved the Zurich rain). On the Artefact side, the labs were led by Zachary Schillaci, PhD, and Artem Kislovskiy. Next stop is Dubai on November 23rd 🇦🇪, and there is more to come with similar sessions planned throughout 2027. ### OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra for faster, better-performing AI agents at half the price

OpenAI Group PBC today released GPT-6.1 Terra, an upgrade to the middle tier model in its lineup of frontier artificial intelligence systems.

The new model, the successor to GTP-5.6 Terra, costs around 50% less while handling computer use tasks faster and with greater accuracy.

Terra is positioned as the everyday model in OpenAI’s lineup, designed for routine work such as reading what’s on a computer screen, clicking through applications, navigating websites and drafting messages. The 50% price cut applies to the model’s standard application programming interface rates, which is what developers pay to integrate GPT-6.1 Terra into their own applications.

According to OpenAI, it’s meant to be a kind of compromise model that’s faster and cheaper for simpler tasks such as filling out forms, interpreting technical drawings, editing videos, creating images and automating repetitive tasks – work that doesn’t require the heft of its more advanced model, GPT-6.1 Sol.

“We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast and efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing,” OpenAI wrote in a blog post introducing the model. “A significant step up from GPT-5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos.”

OpenAI said the model is available now for all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. ChatGPT Work is the agent mode feature within ChatGPT, designed for completing work on behalf of users in third-party applications and browsers, while Codex is OpenAI’s software coding tool.

One concern with GPT-6.1 Terra is that its more advanced capabilities appear to come at a slight cost in terms of safety. In its blog post, OpenAI said that in nearly 30% of simulated runs, Terra went against restrictions to complete tasks using methods it had no authorization to use.

In addition, OpenAI revealed that GPT-6.1 Terra took unauthorized actions in 13.75% of use cases after coming across messages that came from other AI agents. The company’s system card also shows that researchers found evidence that the model understood it was being tested.

Nonetheless, OpenAI said GPT-6.1 Terra did better in some metrics. For instance, on an internal test built using prompts designed to trick models into making mistakes, its rate of factual errors at low reasoning effort fell to just 16.7%, down from 53.6% with GPT-5.6 Terra. When making maximum effort, its rate of factual errors dropped to just 4.3%.

On the Terminal-Bench 4.0 test, which measures coding agents on tasks done through a computer’s command-line terminal, it solved 50.3% of all tasks when using maximum reasoning effort, up from 21.5% with GPT-5.6 Terra. OpenAI said the model completed these tasks around three-times faster on average than more powerful variants such as GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.

The release of Terra follows the debut of GPT-6.1 Sol last month. The lineup also includes a lightweight model variant called GPT-6.1 Luna.

# OpenAI unveils GPT-6.1 Terra, cutting API prices in half

- Input
- 2026-10-27 10:53:00

- Updated
- 2026-10-27 10:53:00

OpenAI said on the 27th that GPT-6.1 Terra would be available through ChatGPT Work, OpenAI Codex and the OpenAI application programming interface (API).

GPT-6.1 Terra combines the ability to understand visual information and perform computer-based tasks with writing and coding skills. It can handle complex tasks such as drafting proposals, converting architectural drawings into three-dimensional (3D) models and recording timecodes for individual scenes in videos. It can also be used for repetitive tasks, such as reading invoice details and entering them into accounting software.

In particular, OpenAI has improved its performance relative to cost. Standard API prices are 50% lower than those for GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol. ChatGPT Work and Codex can also handle more tasks than before within the same usage limits.

It also showed improved results in performance evaluations. On Agent Last Exam, which assesses the ability to perform professional tasks, GPT-6.1 Terra scored 15 percentage points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra at the medium reasoning level. The cost of completing tasks was about one-third as much. It also outperformed its predecessor across all reasoning configurations on MMMU-Pro, a visual reasoning benchmark.

It also reduced AI “hallucinations,” or the generation of information that does not match the facts. In an internal evaluation consisting of questions designed to induce errors, the error rate at the low reasoning level was 16.7%, 36.9 percentage points lower than the previous model’s 53.6%. At the maximum reasoning level, the error rate fell to 4.3%.

Coding performance also improved. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which measures the ability to solve coding problems in a command-line environment, it achieved a solve rate of 50.3% at the maximum reasoning level. That was more than double the previous model’s 21.5%. OpenAI said, however, that GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra are better suited to highly demanding coding tasks.

In terms of safety, GPT-6.1 Terra reached the “Critical” threshold—the highest risk level—in a cybersecurity capability assessment under OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework. Accordingly, it was given the same safeguards as GPT-6 Astra. Its resistance to prompt-injection attacks, which use malicious instructions to manipulate an AI’s tasks, was also strengthened.

GPT-6.1 Terra will be available to users of ChatGPT Work and Codex, as well as ChatGPT Plus, ChatGPT Pro, ChatGPT Enterprise and ChatGPT Edu. API pricing per 1 million tokens is $1 for input, $0.05 for cached input and $5 for output.

# OpenAI Just Dropped a New AI That Can Click Through Your Apps for You

OpenAI has launched GPT-6.1 Terra, a new AI model that can read screens and navigate websites. The model also completes everyday computer tasks three times faster than previous versions. Access began on October 26, 2026, for ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users. Terra works through ChatGPT Work and Codex.

Users can now ask Terra to handle practical tasks like moving invoices from PDFs into accounting software. In addition, the model can draft messages, fill out forms, and navigate websites to place orders on behalf of users. Furthermore, it can interpret technical drawings, edit videos, and even generate images.

The model also works as a coding assistant inside Codex. Specifically, Terra scored 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, which tests command-line programming agents. This marks a sharp jump from GPT-5.6 Terra’s score of 21.5%. However, OpenAI still recommends GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Astra for complex software architecture work.

Terra costs significantly less than other OpenAI models. For developers, the API charges $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens. This represents a 50% price cut from both GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol. As a result, startups and freelancers can run more workflows at lower cost.

The model also makes fewer mistakes than earlier versions. At low reasoning effort, the factual error rate dropped from 53.6% to just 16.7%. At maximum reasoning effort, this number falls to 4.3%.

However, OpenAI’s system card warns about safety concerns. Terra went against restrictions in roughly 30% of simulated test runs to complete its tasks. It also took unauthorized actions in 13.75% of cases after receiving messages from other AI agents. Furthermore, the system card says Terra sometimes noticed the tests.

OpenAI positions Terra as the everyday model for routine work rather than complex reasoning. Still, users should check the system card before running Terra unsupervised in agent workflows.

# OpenAI Introduces GPT-6.1 Terra AI Model With Cost Efficiency, Software Engineering Capabilities Improvements Over GPT-5.6 Terra

OpenAI’s latest GPT-6.1 AI model managed to score higher than GPT-6.1 Sol at a lower cost per token in select tests.

Written by Dhruv Raghav, Edited by Rohan Pal | Updated: 27 October 2026 14:54 IST

Photo Credit: OpenAI

Click Here to Add Gadgets360 As A Trusted Source

Highlights

- GPT-6.1 Terra is available to users in ChatGPT Work and Codex
- GPT-6.1 Terra showed stronger resistance to malicious prompts
- GPT-6.1 Terra reached near GPT-6 Astra performance on select tests

Advertisement

OpenAI introduced its latest AI model, namely GPT-6.1 Terra, on Tuesday. GPT-6.1 Terra is the second AI model in the Sam Altman-led AI giant's GPT-6.1 series, joining the recently released GPT-6.1 Sol. It succeeds the GPT-5.6 Terra AI model, offering improved communication and computer-based tasks over its predecessor. The AI giant also claims that the AI model is better at drafting proposals, interpreting technical drawings, filling out forms, and editing videos. On top of this, OpenAI says that GPT-6.1 Terra presented stronger resistance to malicious prompts in internal testing compared to the GPT-5.6 Terra model.

## OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra Availability, Standard API Pricing

On Tuesday, the Sam Altman-led AI giant announced that its GPT-6.1 Terra AI model is now available to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users. Subscribers can access the latest AI model in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Apart from this, OpenAI says that developers can access GPT-6.1 Terra via the OpenAI API.

In terms of pricing, OpenAI has set the price of the GPT-6.1 Terra standard API at $1 (roughly Rs. 95) per million input tokens, $0.05 (about Rs. 5) per million cached input tokens, and $5 (roughly Rs. 476) per million output tokens. The standard API pricing of the new AI model is 50 percent lower than the prices of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, the company highlighted.

## OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra Capabilities

According to OpenAI, the GPT-6.1 Terra AI model brings improvements over GPT-5.6 Terra in terms of communication and computer-based tasks, like drafting proposals, interpreting technical drawings, filling out forms, and editing videos. On the Agents' Last Exam benchmark test, which tests an AI model's computer-use capabilities, GPT-6.1 Terra scored 15 percentage points higher than its predecessor at medium reasoning effort, at one-third the cost per million tokens.

Interestingly, GPT-6.1 Terra also managed to outperform GPT-6.1 Sol, scoring 60 percentage points against Sol's 58.6 percentage points at Max reasoning effort, while also being notably more cost-efficient. On the MMMU-Pro benchmark for visual reasoning, GPT-6.1 Terra outperformed GPT-5.6, while scoring nearly on par with GPT-6.1 Sol at xHigh reasoning effort.

On OSWorld 2.1, which tests an AI agent's usage of desktop apps to complete multistep tasks, like building a 3D model from a technical drawing, GPT-6.1 Terra scored 53.8 percentage points at low reasoning level, while its predecessor scored lower at max reasoning effort at a higher cost. Further, OpenAI claims that GPT-6.1 Terra also delivered a lower error rate, with reduced hallucinations and factual errors.

At medium reasoning effort, OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra performed nearly on par with Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0, testing the problem-solving capabilities of coding agents. Further, the company says that GPT-6.1 Terra is “more likely to stay within scope and honestly disclose limitations and potential blockers to the user”, in comparison to its predecessor. In OpenAI's internal testing, the AI model showed stronger resistance to “malicious instructions designed to divert” it

# Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 is now available on Google Cloud

October 27, 2026

##### Carolina Parada

VP and Head of Deepmind Robotics

##### Adrian Jones

Applied AI Blackbelt

Earlier this year, we introduced Gemini Robotics 2 — our next-generation intelligence layer enabling robots to think, act, and adapt in the physical world. At the core of this breakthrough is Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 (ER 2), a specialized Gemini model that serves as a robot’s high-level brain. Working across any robot embodiment — from stationary arms to full humanoids — Gemini Robotics ER 2 combines advanced spatial and temporal video understanding with long-horizon planning and built-in safety guardrails. This enables robots to converse naturally with humans, orchestrate low-level action models and hardware APIs, execute multi-minute tasks involving hundreds of decisions, and collaborate across multi-robot teams.

Today, we are bringing this same frontier embodied reasoning model to enterprise production environments: Gemini Robotics ER 2 is now available in public preview on the Gemini platform. For the first time, organizations can pair Google DeepMind’s latest embodied reasoning model for robotics with the enterprise-grade security, multi-agent orchestration, and end-to-end lifecycle management of Google Cloud — making it easier to simulate, evaluate, and deploy safe, adaptive physical AI at scale.

## Powering physical agents for enterprise robotics

Gemini Robotics ER 2 transforms a robot into a physical agent. The model combines deep spatio-temporal reasoning and long-horizon planning, enabling robots to orchestrate steps to complete a task, self-correct, and generalize to novel situations. To build an agentic setup, developers can declare low-level control interfaces — like Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or navigation APIs — as tools, and stream multimodal video, audio, or text directly into the model.

Here is what the model delivers for businesses building and operating robotics:

### 1. Physical task verification, understanding, and self-correction

In physical operations, a robot needs to know whether a step actually succeeded before moving on to the next one. Gemini Robotics ER 2 adapts to new and unfamiliar situations on the fly by reasoning over continuous video feeds. The model:

Classifies task progress into binary status, discrete categories, or continuous scores to improve real-time situational awareness and enable real-time adjustment or iteration on failed steps, without restarting an entire workflow.

Pinpoints the exact video frame where a critical event occurs (such as when to stop pouring a liquid) with 91.3% accuracy and a 0.96-second mean absolute frame distance, running at 4x the execution speed and a fraction of the compute cost of many larger model categories.

It advances our core spatial reasoning capability, including visual question answering and instrument reading. For example, it can read and interpret values across 10+ instrument categories including circular dials, sight glasses, digital displays, linear scales, rulers, and liquid thermometers directly from visual input.

### 2. One intelligence layer across any embodiments

Gemini Robotics ER 2 orchestrates robots of many shapes and sizes, scaling its intelligence from stationary arms and wheeled rovers to quadrupeds and complex forms. It also unlocks multi-robot collaboration, allowing different types of robots to share a semantic understanding of their workspace, divide labor, and hand off tasks to complete workflows a single machine could not do alone.

### 3. Agentic tool orchestration and natural language interaction

Gemini Robotics ER 2 thinks about what comes next while simultaneously orchestrating actions. Developers can declare low-level control interfaces — such as VLA models, navigation APIs, or custom functions — as tools across simulation, real-world robot control, or human tele-operation. Gemini Robotics ER 2 can orchestrate navigation and manipulator movement APIs from natural language commands, allowing the robot to explain its approach while performing an action, and letting operators redirect it without using technical language.

### 4. Build safe, adaptive physical agents in Google Cloud

Developers and enterprise teams use the Gemini platform to simulate, orchestrate, and manage physical agents, which are then deployed to run directly on physical robots at the edge using Google Cloud's scalable infrastructure:

Simulate fast: Test robot behaviors before touching hardware by running simulations in familiar environments like MuJoCo-Warp and NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Then generate synthetic scenarios with multimodal models and auto-label workcell imagery on the Gemini platform.

Train smart: Use Gemini Robotics ER 2's spatial pointing, moment finding, and progress classification to curate and label demonstration videos in Cloud Storage and BigQuery. Then train custom Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models through the Gemini platform, GKE, or Cluster Director.

Operate easily: Deploy Gemini Robotics ER 2 workflows on the Gemini platform with enterprise IAM, security controls, and built-in function calling. Offload latency-sensitive local workloads like SLAM and path planning to factory floors with Google Distributed Cloud, and stream fleet telemetry into BigQuery. Explore the full architecture in Google Cloud Physical AI solutions.

## How customers are building with Gemini Robotics ER 2 in Gemini platform

“We’ve seen exponential growth in customers using AIVI-Learning every month, and Gemini Robotics ER 2 brings them even more value. Video changes what an inspection can be. Spot isn’t just checking whether something looks right in a moment in time, the ability to apply AI models to video opens a whole new world of possibilities.”

Marco da Silva, VP and General Manager of Spot at Boston Dynamics

“DeepReach AI is the real-world skills engine for physical AI. Our hardware and AI platform capture how skilled people work all over the world, and turn it into data flywheel for model training. Gemini Robotics ER 2 gives us accurate task understanding of every recording, to help us find data that matters most — faster and at a far greater scale.”

Chris Liu, Co-founder and CTO at DeepReach

“Advanced reasoning models have the potential to help robots interpret complex environments, plan actions and adapt to changing conditions, opening new possibilities for physical AI. Google’s Gemini Robotics ER 2 model represents an important step in this direction, and we’re excited to be working with Google on exploring how these emerging capabilities can shape the next generation of robotics compute platforms.”

Barrie Mullins, Senior Director of Arm Total Design for Physical AI, at Arm

“We aim to accelerate materials R&D workflows so our scientists can test more ideas, faster. Most lab automation today relies on rigid scripts for single, isolated tasks. By using Gemini Robotics ER 2, we are giving our robots the visual and physical flexibility to work with our existing infrastructure - whether that’s reading a touchscreen on a legacy microwave reactor that has no API, balancing and loading a centrifuge, or moving samples safely through a busy lab. This is the next level that we aspire to reach. This brings us much closer to self-driving labs that can run full experimental campaigns from synthesis to separation, freeing our researchers to focus on thinking up new ideas for discovering new materials.”

Prof. Loh Xian Jun, Executive Director at ASTAR Institute of Materials Research and Engineering (ASTAR IMRE) and Executive Director of MARVEL-AI”

## Get started with Gemini Robotics ER 2 in Gemini platform

Developers and enterprise teams can start building with Gemini Robotics ER 2 today in preview via Model Garden in Gemini platform.

Build in Gemini platform: Visit the Gemini Robotics ER 2 documentation and pricing.

Explore the Developer Guides: Check out sample code and bidirectional streaming guides in the Gemini API Robotics documentation.

Read the Research: Dive into the benchmarks and safety technical report in the Google DeepMind Gemini Robotics ER 2 announcement.

Explore Physical AI on Google Cloud: Visit cloud.google.com/solutions/physical-ai and cloud.google.com/ai to learn how Google Cloud infrastructure supports simulation, training, and deployment.

# Google's Gemini 4 Argon is incredibly smart, but it might not affect you much

When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

Google's latest AI model can untangle millions of lines of code and accelerate quantum computing research, which is great if you happen to spend your afternoons debugging enormous software projects or advancing theoretical physics. For the average Gemini user, the sheer power of the new Gemini 4 Argon model begs the question: why do you need it?

Google has made Gemini 4 Argon readily available in the Gemini app for Google AI Pro or Ultra subscribers. Simply pick it from the list of models available at the top of the conversation. Google brags about the model's advanced reasoning, multi-step problem-solving, and other improvements provided by the sophisticated AI, but it's a little much for helping write an email.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Whether Argon can outperform its predecessors on complicated benchmarks is less interesting than figuring out what to do with all this additional AI power. As AI models become increasingly specialized, we may be approaching a point where the technology is advancing faster than people's ability to understand why they need it.

## Give the big model a big problem

Gemini 4 Argon certainly has potential uses, for instance, in analyzing complicated information scattered across several files. Imagine comparing three health insurance policies with different deductibles, premiums, coverage exclusions, and out-of-pocket limits. A regular Gemini model can already summarize the policies, but Argon's advanced reasoning could become valuable when calculating how different combinations of medical expenses would affect the total annual cost. It would be great at navigating all kinds of potential healthcare scenarios, tracking multiple interacting variables, identifying relevant exceptions, and calculating their consequences.

The same principle applies to any other complicated project, like renovating a house and asking the model to evaluate contractor estimates, material costs, and architectural plans for inconsistencies and potential price overruns. Argon 4 might help when determining how a delayed electrical inspection affects several subsequent jobs and the overall budget.

It could also be useful in learning complicated academic subjects that incorporate a lot of interconnected concepts, such as advanced math. All of that is still only potentially better than simply using the less powerful models. It might be as complicated to work out when Argon 4 is necessary as the very projects for which the model is best suited.

## Overthinking AI

It sometimes feels ridiculous how Google is building models capable of tackling extraordinary scientific and engineering challenges, then placing them in the same interface people use to request pancake recipes. The technology is becoming increasingly sophisticated, yet the reasons to choose one model over another remain vague.

Advertisement

Advertisement

This is hardly unique to Google. OpenAI and Anthropic have their own incredibly powerful models that seem ill-suited to the average user. The most powerful model isn't always going to be the most useful. Asking Gemini to rewrite an email or suggest dinner ideas probably doesn't require Argon's additional reasoning capabilities. A faster model might deliver an equally useful answer faster. Even the more complicated examples aren't necessarily beyond ordinary Gemini models. Argon's advantage would need to come from handling unusually complicated combinations of constraints.

The challenge for Google is that users can't easily recognize which assignments justify a more powerful model. In that case, the model picker becomes an annoyance and not a feature.

Right now, most Gemini users should stick to the less intense models and reserve Gemini 4 Argon for assignments where they would struggle. Argon 4 is apparently a remarkable technical achievement with huge possible benefits in some research, but I don't need something capable of solving quantum computing problems on an everyday basis. AI developers have become very good at building models capable of extraordinary work, but the most impressive feat would be explaining when ordinary people actually need them.

# 8 examples of Gemini 4 Argon in action

Kimberly Fusaro

Contributor

Listen to article

This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental

Our newest model, Gemini 4 Argon, was built to solve your hardest problems. By tackling complex, real-world tasks and taking on high-stakes work that used to require months of manual effort, it's fundamentally changing the way we work and build at Google — and it can do the same for you. Go ahead and hand over dense research materials, raw photos, and multi-step projects. Argon will reason, code, and coordinate tools to deliver what you need.

From deep research to interactive 3D design, here are eight examples of what our most intelligent model yet can do.

## Handling complex tasks

Using advanced reasoning and multimodal capabilities, Gemini 4 Argon excels in deep comprehension and long-horizon workflows. From a short prompt and with zero assets or libraries, Argon wrote 5,000 lines of math to render a 3D sunlit library from scratch — and then made a video about the process.

## Making interactive tools and playable 3D games

Googlers have used Argon to prototype complex 3D visualizations, high-fidelity games, and interactive animations. When prompted to build an app to overlay shapes across videos, Gemini 4 Argon in the Gemini app generated a custom audiovisual tool that traces musical scale lines from frame to frame. The motion of the video triggers musical notes, creating a dynamic audio composition.

To turn your world into an interactive game, start with photos of a physical space and our AI Studio how-to. We used Argon in Antigravity to orchestrate subagents, Blender MCP, and Nano Banana to transform pictures of a real desk into a playable 3D track.

## Optimizing workflows

Argon combines frontier reasoning, deep visual perception, expanded knowledge, and stronger writing capabilities to help with high-stakes professional workflows. Given a custom slides template and more than 80,000 raw files from NASA — including weather logs and engineering, health, and science data accumulated across 72 flights on Mars — Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity was able to parse information, organize insights, and turn it all into an executive-ready deck with clear visual narratives.

## Building engaging visuals

Gemini 4 Argon is especially strong when work requires visual understanding. When prompted to make dense academic chapters come alive, Argon used Nano Banana and Veo to transform the scientific concepts in a PDF into an illustrated animation of key moments in the Gemini app.

To create an unforgettable science explainer in Antigravity, Argon generated a self-navigating 3D periodic table with animated atoms choreographed with frame-accurate audio timing to the rapid-fire lyrics of “The Elements” by Tom Lehrer.

## Generating lifelike textures

Argon brings a deeper understanding of real-time 3D rendering, lighting and shading, and interactive physics simulation. This allows Argon in Antigravity to code a custom “fur engine” with studio-grade hair dynamics, generating visually rich fur that grows and moves as a character does.

We also used Argon in Antigravity to create an interactive musical “G” with fluid physics and reactive sound.

Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and Gemini platform, for Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in Google Antigravity, and Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.

# Springer Nature and Google DeepMind collaborate to enhance the peer review experience

London, Berlin, New York -- 26th October 2026. Peer reviewers play an essential role in safeguarding the quality and integrity of published research. With this in mind, Springer Nature and Google DeepMind are announcing a research partnership to co-design an AI peer review assistant to explore how technology can help create a more rewarding reviewer experience. The assistant will help researchers to review papers more effectively, support them in navigating manuscripts, and identify areas that may need closer attention so they can spend more time on the questions that require specialist scientific judgement.

The partnership brings together Springer Nature's expertise in managing peer review and Google DeepMind's frontier Gemini models. Building on Google's experience in developing proven agentic research tools like ScholarPeer and Deep Review, the new assistant helps reviewers analyse large amounts of text, charts, and figures.

The prototype assistant currently being tested will help re-envision peer review as an interactive experience that uses AI to empower scientific experts while keeping expert human judgment at the centre of the process. This project is part of Springer Nature's ongoing commitment to deliver a more frictionless publishing process for authors and peer reviewers which includes its in-house platform, Snapp.

Saskia Steinacker, Chief Product Officer, Springer Nature said:

"The expertise and judgement of reviewers are fundamental to peer review. As research grows in volume and complexity, we have an opportunity to explore how AI can responsibly support that expertise, helping reviewers focus their time where it matters most and on the questions that require specialist scientific judgement. For us, innovation and trust have to go hand in hand. That means testing what AI can add while being clear about where responsibility remains."

The system is built using Google's open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK). It runs solely in Springer Nature's private, secure Gemini Enterprise platform. This means any content used to develop and test the AI peer reviewer assistant remains within Springer Nature's secure environment, ensuring author and reviewer confidentiality is maintained throughout.

Seshu Ajjarapu, Senior Director, Applied AI, at Google DeepMind, said:

"Unlocking scientific discovery requires a peer-review experience that is both rigorous and in sync with the pace of research. This partnership brings together Springer Nature's scientific publishing expertise and Google DeepMind's frontier research. Together, we are building a platform that relieves the strain of growing submission volumes while strictly upholding the editorial standards of the world's leading journals. It's a prime example of how AI can strengthen the foundational structures of modern science."

The initiative reflects Springer Nature's broader commitment to using AI responsibly across research and publishing: human first, AI second. Further updates will be shared as testing progresses and development continues. More on the publishers' approach to AI use and guidance for its author, editor and research community can be found here.

### About Springer Nature

Springer Nature is one of the leading publishers of research in the world. We publish the largest number of journals and books and are a pioneer in open research. Through our leading brands, trusted for more than 180 years, we provide technology-enabled products, platforms and services that help researchers to uncover new ideas and share their discoveries, health professionals to stay at the forefront of medical science, and educators to advance learning. We are proud to be part of progress, working together with the communities we serve to share knowledge and bring greater understanding to the world. For more information, please visit about.springernature.com and follow Springer Nature.

### About Google DeepMind

Google DeepMind is a world-leading AI research lab with British heritage and an international team, committed to building AI responsibly, delivering scientific breakthroughs, and creating products that improve billions of lives. The team's breakthroughs over the last decade include AlphaGo - the first computer program to defeat a Go world champion, Transformers - neural networks that underpin all modern language models, AlphaFold - an AI model that can accurately predict the structure and interactions of proteins, DNA, RNA, ligands and more, and Gemini, a family of versatile AI models built from the ground up for multimodality, seamlessly combining and understanding text, code, images, audio and video.

# Google Deepmind's Genie 4 puts a modern spin on agent designs that predate LLMs

## Key Points

- Google Deepmind has introduced Genie 4, an interactive world model that calculates environments frame by frame in real time and, for the first time, directly generates matching background audio and character dialogue.
- Gemini models steer events in the background, planning multistep tasks and continuously adapting the simulated world to user text prompts and changing conditions.
- Genie 4 is still an experimental research model with limitations in longer sessions and complex physics. Access is limited to select testers for now and will later expand to Google AI Ultra subscribers.

Genie 4 is supposed to simulate interactive worlds in real time, including sound and talking characters. Gemini models plan in the background what happens next in the simulation. Only select testers can try the world model for now.

Google Deepmind has introduced Genie 4, the successor to Genie 3, which the company showed in August 2025. The world model doesn't produce finished videos but calculates a scene frame by frame, reacting to input as it goes. Users move through the scene with the keyboard and steer events with text prompts.

According to Deepmind, Genie 4 is the company's first real-time world model that generates sound directly. The company says each world has its own background audio, such as wind in the trees. Genie 4 also handles dialogue, with characters that are supposed to talk to each other and react in real time to user input or events.

Deepmind sees the biggest gain in realism in how the model renders people. Characters are supposed to move naturally and react to their surroundings, and users should be able to control them directly.

## Gemini models plan ahead to keep the world coherent

According to Deepmind, Genie 4 builds on capabilities of the video model Gemini Omni so the world looks and behaves realistically. Other Gemini models help plan the simulation to keep it consistent.

If a user changes the weather with a text prompt, Gemini is supposed to adapt the instruction to the running scene. Deepmind says Gemini also steers events between inputs so the world keeps developing in a way that makes sense.

Deepmind explains the process with multistep tasks. Gemini 3.8 Flash watches the scene continuously, breaks a goal into steps, and uses new frames to check whether each step worked. If the world changes or the user steps in, the model adjusts its plan.

Deepmind is also testing Gemini 4 Argon to tie its Genie work to its robotics research, Gemini Robotics. In one demo, Argon breaks the task of playing checkers into steps. Genie 4 gets these as text instructions and uses them to simulate Apptronik's humanoid robot Apollo playing the game, with no real robot involved.

## Longer sessions still trip up the model

Deepmind calls Genie 4 an early, experimental model. According to the company, the world stays consistent over short sessions, but visual details can shift and objects don't always persist in longer simulations or after several complex prompt changes.

Deepmind says it's still researching complex physical interactions, accurate real-time sound, and readable text.

For now, Genie 4 is only available to select testers as a research preview. It's set to reach Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Project Genie web app soon, along with partners who have early access to the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

Google says all videos and audio tracks will carry its SynthID watermark, which invisibly marks AI-generated content.

Once they mature, world models could serve as training environments where robots and AI agents learn from simulated experience rather than just from data. Deepmind sees pairing Gemini with Genie as an early step toward hybrid world models that combine the reasoning of language and code models with pixel-level simulation.

# Meta Platform seeks to raise $95 billion through stock offering in largest ever funding round for AI expansion

Bobins Vayalil Abraham

Published27 Oct 2026, 08:05 AM IST

Advertisement

Meta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram, and Facebook, on Monday said it plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, as it continues with its aggressive AI infrastructure expansion. According to Meta, it will initially raise $35 billion in underwritten public equity offerings, before raising an additional $60 billion with an at-the-market program.

Advertisement

## ‘To support emerging AI opportunities’

The company will launch the larger share sale program after its new non-voting Class C shares begin trading, which is expected in the first quarter of 2027, but said it has not yet finalized its timing and terms of the sale, a Reuters report said.

According to Meta, the planned investments will support “emerging AI opportunities” including its family of apps, its AI agent Muse and its data center business.

It plans to balance funding for these investments through a mix of operating cash flow, investment-grade debt, partnerships and equity capital, the company said.

Meta has been pouring money into chips and data centers to compete better with OpenAI and Anthropic.

"We expect investors to continue to question the financing and potential for future capital raises," William Blair analysts were quoted as saying by Reuters.

Advertisement

"Overall, we believe the financing reinforces both Meta's confidence in the long-term returns from AI investment and the increasingly capital-intensive nature of pursuing that opportunity."

## Growing AI investments

Meta's fundraising plan, among the biggest by an AI company, has also drawn interest of up to $5 billion in total from Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom for Class A shares.

Their funding interest adds to concerns about an increasingly circular flow of capital in the AI industry, as chip suppliers help finance the expansion of one of their biggest customers. Meta has been pouring money into chips and data centers to compete better with OpenAI and Anthropic.

## Where does Meta stand in AI race?

Despite trailing far behind the market leaders like OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude and Google’s Gemini, Meta has been aggressively pushing ahead with its AI expansion.

Advertisement

Meta’s AI offerings include the Llama language model and the recently introduced virtual assistant, Muse. According to data from Resourcera, Meta AI has grown faster than almost any technology product in history. In just two years, it went from 213 million users in January 2024 to over 1.2 billion monthly active users by January 2026, with a 464% increase.

This makes it the second-largest AI assistant worldwide, only behind ChatGPT, holding a 15 to 20% share of the global AI market.

Meta has committed to spend about $825 billion in the future, primarily driven by its growing investments in data centers, AI-related infrastructure and cloud computing power.

Meta.content:
# Llama 4 deployment priorities for local inference

Meta’s Llama 4 models offer efficient local enterprise deployment through mixture-of-experts architectures. Llama 4 Maverick outperforms GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash on several benchmarks while fitting on a single NVIDIA H100 DGX host.

## Efficiency through mixture of experts

I recommend Llama 4 Scout for businesses that require high efficiency on limited hardware. Meta designed Llama 4 Scout with 17 billion active parameters and 109 billion total parameters. This model fits on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU with 4-bit quantization. The mixture-of-experts architecture activates only 16 experts per token. Llama 4 Maverick uses 128 routed experts and 1 shared expert to achieve high performance. Llama 4 Maverick provides 17 billion active parameters and 128 experts, which permits the model to beat GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash across many benchmarks and maintains a high performance to cost ratio for enterprises. Meta developed these models using distillation from Llama 4 Behemoth. Behemoth contains 288 billion active parameters and 16 experts. While Behemoth remains in training, it achieved 390 TFLOPs per GPU with FP8 precision. Meta used MetaP hyperparameter tuning to set per-layer learning rates and initialization scales. This technique ensures better generalization across model width and depth. The training process for the Llama 4 family used more than 30 trillion tokens. This data mixture included text, image, and video datasets.

Model | Active Parameters | Total Parameters | Context Length | Hardware Requirement 
---|---|---|---|---
Llama 4 Scout | 17B | 109B | 10M tokens | Single NVIDIA H100 
Llama 4 Maverick | 17B | 400B | 1M tokens | Single NVIDIA H100 DGX 
Llama 4 Behemoth | 288B | ~2T | N/A | N/A 

## Context depth and model performance

Llama 4 Maverick delivers high performance across text and image understanding. It achieves an ELO of 1417 on LMArena for chat. Maverick outperforms GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash on coding, reasoning, and image benchmarks. It also beats Gemini 2.0 in MathVista and MMLU-Vision. Maverick costs between $0.19 and $0.49 per 1 million tokens. The Scout model provides a 10 million token context window. This exceeds the 2 million token window of Gemini 2.0. The Scout model also beats Gemma 3 and Mistral 3.1 on several benchmarks. Both models use early fusion to combine text and vision tokens. This architecture allows the model to reason across modalities. Maverick shows 85-92% accuracy on fields requiring complex logic in Box AI evaluations. Maverick also achieves 80.5 in MMLU Pro and 69.8 in GPQA Diamond. Maverick outperforms Llama 3.3 70B in both speed and quality. The Scout model allows for reasoning over massive codebases because of its 10 million token window. This capability exceeds the 128k token limit seen in some third-party implementations. Maverick is a choice for building production-grade assistants with improved instruction following.

## Control and governance in local environments

Enterprises download Llama 4 weights to run models on their own infrastructure or through managed providers. This choice allows organizations to keep data on-premises and fine-tune models on proprietary data. You already know that proprietary APIs send data to third parties. Self-hosting shifts responsibility for security, monitoring, and auditing to the deploying organization. Organizations face challenges such as shadow AI proliferation and missing audit trails when they deploy these models. Llama 4 Maverick fits in a single NVIDIA H100 DGX host. Llama 4 Scout works on a single NVIDIA H100. Some developers criticized Meta because the LMArena version differed from the version available for download. Will Meta release a reasoning model to address developer concerns about agentic capabilities? Organizations must manage identity systems to recognize autonomous agents as distinct principals. They also require monitoring to track prompts and tool calls throughout the interaction lifecycle. Using Llama 4 requires organizations to manage credentials and access control to prevent unauthorized access. Developers can deploy Llama 4 Scout on 8x H100 GPUs with a 200k token context window. They can also use 4x H100 GPUs to reduce costs with a lower context window capacity. Maverick requires 8x H200 GPUs for a 100k token context window.

Meta.content:
# Nvidia invests $3 billion in Meta, deepens Muse partnership

Nvidia is investing 3 billion dollar in Meta. The two companies are also working more tightly together on Meta’s Muse AI models and agents. Meta is set to deploy more Vera Rubin systems for the Muse venture, using the Arm-based Nvidia Vera CPUs and networking equipment from Nvidia.

Both parties are seeking to optimize Muse workflows for training and inference to improve performance and lower the total cost of ownership. Nvidia notes the impressive capabilities and popularity from the Muse models, which have thrusted Meta back into the AI conversation after a long absence.

Muse is a relatively new effort and distinct from the erstwhile Llama models. The family started with Muse Spark back in April, a multimodal reasoning model from Meta Superintelligence Labs that handles text, images, external tools and multiple AI agents. Meta went on to launch Muse in September. It acts as a personal agent that can book travel, fill in forms and make purchases on behalf of its user.

Mark Zuckerberg isn’t shy about the ambition, wholly distinct from the improvised open-weight sensation that Llama became in 2023-24. “Muse is how we bring personal superintelligence to everyone,” he said.

## Vera Rubin and agent security

For infrastructure, Meta will expand its deployment of Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs. The focus here, as common to Arm-based systems, is on performance per watt. Spectrum-X Ethernet and BlueField-4 will improve network efficiency and throughput through specialized silicon. The expansion is a continuation of a multiyear, multigenerational deal that covered millions of Blackwell and Rubin GPUs. Meta doesn’t rely on Nvidia alone, though. It also works with AMD, custom chips and external cloud providers, and it is looking into selling its excess compute capacity.

Another avenue of cooperation revolves around agent security. Meta is saying it is considering the adoption of Nvidia’s OpenShell Reference Architecture. This would include using OpenShell as a runtime for safe deployment and Sentry for monitoring agent behavior.

## Part of a 95 billion dollar fundraise

Nvidia is but one investor Meta is planning to align with its plans, as it seeks to raise up to 95 billion dollars. That includes roughly 35 billion dollar in immediate offerings and a 60 billion dollar at-the-market share program. This would only kick in by early 2027. Much of that money will almost immediately be out the door as well, as the company expects capital expenditures of 135-145 billion dollar in 2026. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom had already indicated an interest in buying up to 5 billion dollars of Meta stock combined.

# Your First API Call

The DeepSeek API uses an API format compatible with OpenAI/Anthropic. By modifying the configuration, you can use the OpenAI/Anthropic SDK or softwares compatible with the OpenAI/Anthropic API to access the DeepSeek API.

PARAM | VALUE 
---|---
base_url (OpenAI) | https://api.deepseek.com 
base_url (Anthropic) | https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic 
api_key | apply for an API key 
model | deepseek-flash(1)deepseek-v4-pro 

(1) Usedeepseek-flash as the model name. It is now served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, and the calling method remains unchanged. The legacy names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted, but the corresponding models have been retired; their requests are served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and billed at the Flash price.

## Integrate with Agent Tools

DeepSeek Harness is now in developer preview for agent harness developers worldwide. See the DeepSeek Harness Guide for details.

The DeepSeek API is supported by many popular AI agent and coding assistant tools. If you use tools like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or OpenCode, you can use DeepSeek as the backend model directly — no code required.

See the Agent Integrations Guide for details.

## Invoke The Chat API

Once you have obtained an API key, you can access the DeepSeek model using the following example scripts in the OpenAI API format. This is a non-stream example, you can set thestream parameter to true to get stream response.

For examples using the Anthropic API format, please refer to Anthropic API.

- curl
- python
- nodejs

curl https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
        "model": "deepseek-flash",
        "messages": [
          {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
          {"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}
        ],
        "thinking": {"type": "enabled"},
        "reasoning_effort": "high",
        "stream": false
      }'
# Please install OpenAI SDK first: `pip3 install openai`
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ.get('DEEPSEEK_API_KEY'),
    base_url="https://api.deepseek.com",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="deepseek-flash",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant"},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
    ],
    stream=False,
    reasoning_effort="high",
    extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "enabled"}},
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
// Please install OpenAI SDK first: `npm install openai`

import OpenAI from "openai";

const openai = new OpenAI({
        baseURL: 'https://api.deepseek.com',
        apiKey: process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY,
});

async function main() {
  const completion = await openai.chat.completions.create({
    messages: [{ role: "system", content: "You are a helpful assistant." }],
    model: "deepseek-flash",
    thinking: {"type": "enabled"},
    reasoning_effort: "high",
    stream: false,
  });

  console.log(completion.choices[0].message.content);
}

main();

# DeepSeek为什么能登顶全球第一？

中国战略新兴产业融媒体记者 陈虹江

据每日经济新闻，OpenRouter最新数据测算，上周（10月19日至25日）全球AI大模型总调用量为188万亿Token，环比增长14.63%。全球调用量排名前五均为中国AI大模型。DeepSeekV4.1-Flash-1017位居第一，周调用量达33. 6万亿Token，环比增长801%。 

在上周上榜的AI大模型中，中国AI大模型周调用量达93.54万亿Token，环比增长18.14%；同期美国AI大模型周调用量为22.47万亿Token，环比增长29.44%。中国大模型周调用量连续二十六周超过美国，稳居全球首位。

以DeepSeek为代表的中国AI大模型公司阶段领先是来自产品技术、成本、体验、开源策略?还是在国内外的行业市场环境、相关政策差异下“长”出来的？

**01**

**从“会聊天”到“会干活”**

DeepSeek的登顶，表面看是调用量的成绩，底层是技术路线的进步。

早期大模型在工作场景中的应用，主要停留在“生成辅助”层面。撰写初稿、补全代码、翻译文本。其本质是一个高效的文本生成器，用户需要提供明确的指令和上下文，模型输出一段文本供人工进一步加工。

2026年以来，这一边界正在被突破。技术进步最显著的方向，是从对话能力转向Agent能力。模型不再只是“回答问题”，而是开始“操作计算机完成任务”。

智谱GLM-5.1、MiniMax M3、阶跃Step 5、字节豆包2.1 Pro 等新一代模型，都在工具调用、终端操作、代码生成等Agent能力上做了重点投入。Terminal-Bench（终端操作）、ProgramBench（编程任务）、BFCL（工具调用）等基准测试上的分数持续提升，意味着模型开始具备“读文件、跑命令、调试程序、生成项目”的实际生产力。

**麦肯锡《 The State of AI 2026》全球调研****中指出** 大型企业（年收入超10亿美元）在至少一项业务职能中规模化部署AI智能体的比例，从2025年的27%跃升至 2026年的40%。其中约31%的大型企业已在规模化部署**软件编码智能体** 。聊天机器人仍是当前部署最广泛的AI应用形态。

另外，百万级Token的上下文窗口，让模型可以一次性读完一个代码仓库、一份十万字合同、一整本书。当模型能“看到”完整的项目结构，它的Agent行为就从“单步操作”进化到“多步规划”。

在具体工作场景中，Agent智能体已经落实到多个领域。

在软件工程领域，传统的工作流是“需求分析、架构设计、代码编写、测试调试”。大模型的引入，使得代码编写和测试调试环节的执行成本大幅降低，开发者的注意力配置从“代码实现”向“架构设计与质量评审”转移。

在内容生产领域，文案撰写、报告初稿、竞品分析整理等“格式化认知劳动”被模型高效完成，内容工作者的角色从“创作者”转变为“编辑与策展者”负责调性把控、事实核查和价值判断。

在数据分析领域，数据提取和初步统计的自动化，使分析师的工作重心从“数据获取"”转向“数据解读与业务洞察”。这符合信息系统研究中的经典判断：**当数据获取成本趋零，数据解释的价值上升****。**

**02**

**用“构架创新”绕开“堆算力”**

DeepSeek在新版本打出的口号，精准切中了开发者社区的痛点。从写代码到做项目，AI编程的门槛被进一步拉低。新版本在“终端操作”和“软件逆向”两个维度上的进步最为显著，模型不再只是“写代码的助手”，而是开始具备“操作计算机完成任务”的Agent能力。

这次升级是“无感切换”。开发者无需修改任何代码，无需承担额外成本，即可在原有API入口获得能力更强的模型。这种“免费升级+性能跃升”的组合，直接触发了调用量的爆发式迁移。

清华大学智能产业研究院院长张亚勤指出，DeepSeek并不是通过“蒸馏”别人的模型来实现的。它在算法和架构上有很多创新，比如MLA结构、MoE专家混合，还有KV Compression 等等。创新点非常多，绝不仅仅是借鉴现有方法。

全球大模型行业最早探索MoE的不是中国公司。Google的Switch Transformer、Meta的Mixtral都做过尝试。但真正把MoE做到“高性价比”并跑通商业闭环的，是中国公司。

两年前，MoE还是大模型领域的小众路线。到2026年，中国头部大模型公司纷纷看向了MoE。

智谱GLM-5.1是一个典型案例：总参数量7540亿，但推理时只激活约400亿参数，超过94%的参数在每次推理时处于“休眠”状态。用一个通俗的比喻：一个公司有256个专家顾问，每次开会只叫最懂当前议题的8个人来，而不是把所有人都拉到会议室。这种设计让GLM-5.1在保持庞大知识容量的同时，把单次推理的计算成本压到极低。

阿里巴巴通义千问Qwen3.5则是：397B总参数、17B激活，采用MoE与线性注意力（Gated Delta Networks）混合架构，原生支持视觉-语言多模态，语言和方言支持从119种扩展到201种。MoE在这里不再只是“省算力”的工具，而是与新注意力机制结合，成为提升模型效率的底层框架。

元脑Yuan3.0 Ultra则在MoE的专家调度算法上做了创新：1010B 总参数、68.8B 激活，提出 Layer-Adaptive Expert Pruning（LAEP）算法，在预训练阶段就对专家进行自适应剪枝，进一步提升了训练和推理效率。

MiniMax、阶跃星辰 Step 系列、字节豆包Seed系列，也都选择了MoE路线。央广网在2026年初的行业观察中总结道：MoE架构、多模态融合、超长上下文理解功能几乎成为标配，评估模型也从“参数越大越好”转变为“运行越高效越好”。

中国大模型的技术进步，还受益于独特的开源生态。Hugging Face 2026 春季报告显示，全球41%的大模型下载量来自中国研发的模型。DeepSeek、Qwen（通义千问）、GLM 等模型持续开源，形成了巨大的全球开发者社区。

开源不是“只投入、无回报”，而是技术进化的加速器。全球开发者在使用过程中发现 bug、提出改进建议、贡献微调方案，这些反馈回流到模型团队，反过来推动模型快速迭代。OpenRouter平台上开源模型词元处理比例从年初的 34%跃升至65%，超过500家机构从专有模型切换到开源模型。这个过程中，中国模型团队获得了海量真实场景的反馈数据。

**算法 -框架****-****硬件协同设计** 是另一个关键。中国公司不是在英伟达提供的软件栈上做“应用层优化”，而是从算子级、通信库级、集群调度级全链路重新设计。当别人还在用标准CUDA框架跑训练时，国内大模型团队已经在自定义FP8算子、优化AllReduce通信、调整GPU集群拓扑。这种深度优化的结果是：同样的GPU 数量，中国公司能跑出更高的利用率。

技术架构决定了模型能否提高效率，那么市场竞争决定了这种效率能否被用户感知。

**03**

**为什么中国大模型市场能跑出来？**

**价格差决定了 Token消耗量级。**同一笔API预算，买GPT-5.5可能只够跑几亿Token，买DeepSeek Flash能跑出几十亿甚至上百亿Token。虎嗅网算过一笔账：DeepSeek V4 Flash 处理一个标准任务约0.02美元，同档美国模型要2.75美元，差出100多倍。

北京物联网智能技术应用协会副会长、中关村大数据产业联盟副秘书长颜阳对Token定价逻辑指出：Token 是模型处理信息的计量单位，用户实际购买的是以Token计量的智能服务。不同模型处理同一段内容，词元数量和解决问题的能力都不同，不能像 “一度电”那样去比价。 他提出Token定价受成本、供需和价值三方面影响：成本端含芯片折旧、电力与研发回收；供需取决于高峰拥堵与资源紧张；价值则看模型能否解决复杂问题、提供稳定服务。

针对中外价格悬殊，颜阳提醒不能简单说“中国便宜、国外贵”，比较须做到同任务、同质量、同服务条件。他指出中国优势在于开放模型生态活跃、应用场景丰富，但高端算力可获得性和大规模稳定服务能力仍是短板。“开源让更多人有机会提供智能，算力决定能够提供多少智能，应用决定这些智能值多少钱。”他强调，中国应把成本优势进一步转化为效果优势和服务优势。

**成本底座不同。** 中国大模型的成本优势，还体现在上游算力基础设施的布局上。华龙证券研报指出，中国西部低廉的绿色电力成本是重要的底层支撑。在“东数西算”工程的推动下，贵州、内蒙古、宁夏等西部地区建设了大量数据中心，利用当地丰富的风电、光伏等绿色电力资源，大幅降低了算力的单位用电成本。

另外，国产算力芯片的逐步成熟也在降低国产GPU的进口成本占比。虽然DeepSeek的训练仍主要依赖英伟达H800芯片，但在推理端，国产芯片的适配和优化正在取得进展。当训练成本已经被架构创新压缩到极低水平，推理端的成本优化空间就更大。

**在上游成本优势的基础上，大模型厂商展开了激烈的 “卷成本”，而****美国市场缺乏降价动力。** 中国头部模型厂商，DeepSeek、MiniMax、智谱、阶跃星辰，不约而同走MoE 架构+极致工程优化路线，每一家降价都倒逼其他家跟进，整个行业的成本曲线持续下移。而美国市场是OpenAI和 Anthropic两家占大头，都瞄准高毛利企业客户，没有强烈的价格竞争压力。直到中国模型进入美国市场，OpenAI才在今年连续两轮降价。

东方财富证券研报写到，DeepSeek今年以来经历了“降价-峰谷计价-整体上调”的三步演化，结合海外市场近一年从“普降”到“旗舰涨价”再到“分层促销”的定价变化，标志着国产模型有望从粗放式价格战转向高质量竞争。

**下游应用端的 “人口基数”差异。**中国有海量中小企业和个人开发者，微信、飞书、钉钉等平台触达亿级用户，AI应用场景从编程助手到文档处理到智能客服全面铺开。火山方舟平台上已有110万企业和个人用户，年调用量超万亿Token的企业达200家。而美国模型主要服务少数大型企业客户，客单价高但调用频次和用户基数有限。

一句总结，美国模型走的是“精品高毛利”路线，服务少数大客户；中国模型走的是 “普惠大规模”路线，靠极低成本覆盖海量用户和场景。调用量是 “薄利多销”的结果，不代表模型能力全面超越，但在AI基础设施早期阶段，规模本身就是护城河。

**从政策层面看，中国在推应用，美国在管安全。** 10月23日国务院办公厅对外发布的《关于适应人工智能技术发展助力构建就业友好型发展方式的意见》部署了6个方面18项主要任务。指出拓展新兴领域人工智能就业新空间，培育中小微企业稳岗扩岗新动能，创造人工智能领域就业创业新模式，加快开发人工智能领域新职业。完善人机协同下的劳动者权益、灵活就业社保和收入分配机制。建立 AI 就业影响监测体系和风险应对机制。

在6月上旬美国总统特朗普签署了“促进先进人工智能创新与安全”行政令。该行政令是特朗普政府在“创新优先”与“国家安全关切”之间妥协的产物。行政令明确对前沿模型网络不设强制许可或预先批准，但保留对其能力的评估机制。美国人工智能企业在公开发布前沿模型前，需“自愿”向政府提供模型并进行“前置安全评估”。

A flagship MoE large model with 1.6 trillion parameters and 49 billion activated parameters, natively supporting context lengths of up to one million tokens. Trained on a vast corpus of high-quality data, it excels in advanced mathematical reasoning, complex logical inference, specialized coding, and deep analysis of long-form text, making it well-suited for demanding applications such as cutting-edge research, sophisticated office workflows, and advanced AI agents.

DeepSeek.description: DeepSeek在与投资者洽谈期间至少两次上调融资目标，融资规模从最初计划的500亿元增至800亿元，最终达到约1000亿元。加上此前约510亿元首轮融资，DeepSeek年内两轮融资累计约1500亿元，投前估值约5000亿元，并为科创板IPO铺路。
DeepSeek.content:
\# 千亿元融资展现中国AI进取心

一禁、一开、一融，指向同一个命题：在围堵与竞逐并起的全球AI牌桌上，中国大模型拿什么下注未来？

千亿融资的体量本身就是一个信号。DeepSeek在与投资者洽谈期间至少两次上调融资目标，融资规模从最初计划的500亿元增至800亿元，最终达到约1000亿元。加上此前约510亿元首轮融资，DeepSeek年内两轮融资累计约1500亿元，投前估值约5000亿元，并为科创板IPO铺路。

这笔钱更重的分量在于出钱的人。此轮融资，投资者有芯片、汽车、新能源、互联网平台等多领域巨头。产业资本而非单纯金融资本在重注DeepSeek，说明其发展路线已获得产业链上下游认同，获得中国制造与数字经济的双重背书，市场已将其视为带动国产算力、能源、应用生态共同运转的枢纽。

美国禁令的出台，恰恰从反面印证了这一枢纽地位。美国国土安全部不仅禁止联邦机构直接采购DeepSeek，还“连坐”使用DeepSeek模型开发的第三方衍生产品。这种“穿透式”排除手法，说明美方担心DeepSeek开源模型渗透进整个软件供应链的潜力。

禁令越彻底，越暴露出焦虑。当中国模型以开源姿态进入全球开发者的工具箱，传统的封堵手段正在失效。美国封得住机构账户，封不住开源的代码本身。更讽刺的是，越是把开源技术贴上国别标签，越说明竞争的天平已不偏向筑墙者一边。

开源与禁令同框，更显自信与张力。DeepSeek全面开放DeepInfer，意味着任何企业都可以在英伟达或昇腾平台上以更低成本部署接近官方水准的推理服务。将这样的核心技术公之于众，看似削弱了自身的技术壁垒，实则做大了整个生态的基数。

开源是一种战略：你关上一扇门，我就把钥匙发给所有人。中小企业不必从零搭建推理优化能力，高校研究团队可以在昇腾平台上验证自己的模型设计，DeepSeek则获得一个以自身技术栈为参照系的开发者网络。网络效应一旦形成，其黏性远非几项专利可比。

在全球AI资源向少数闭源巨头集中时，DeepSeek的选择让更多国家、更多企业、更多开发者有机会参与这场技术革命。这种技术平权，与中国在新能源、电动汽车等领域的全球化路径一脉相承。我们不靠封锁别人建立优势，而靠开放生态赢得世界。

当然，前路并非坦途，清醒同样必要。美国联邦政府的直接订单本就不是DeepSeek的主场，真正的考题是寒蝉效应下的盟友跟进、出海合规与数据信任。此外，与OpenAI、Anthropic等美国公司累计逾千亿美元的融资体量相比，中国头部AI公司仍然差着一个数量级，下一代DeepSeek模型的原创性突破、商业化纵深与算力供给，都是绕不开的硬仗。

融资增实力，开源定路线，普惠赢人心。在有人忙着筑墙的地方选择架桥，把最先进的技术做成人人可及的公共产品，这份在压力下仍昂然向前的姿态，正是中国AI企业最可贵的进取心。（本文来源：经济日报 作者：佘惠敏）

# DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017：完整项目开发更强，搜索与抓取 API 开放

原创 于 2026-10-27 09:50:43 发布 · 72 阅读

·   1
·   2  ·

版权声明：本文为博主原创文章，遵循 CC 4.0 BY-SA 版权协议，转载请附上原文出处链接和本声明。

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017显著提升编程与Agent能力，Terminal-Bench 4.0达42.3，DeepSWE通过率升至77%，任务费用降低约60%。支持百万token上下文，采用CED+MoE+CSA2架构优化KV缓存，显存占用大幅下降。同步开放Search与Fetch API，支持网页搜索与正文抓取，适用于RAG和代码Agent场景，按成功请求计费。

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 在编程与 Agent 能力上全面提升：Terminal-Bench 4.0 从 31.2 升至 42.3，DeepSWE v1.1 通过率升至 77%，每任务费用降低约六成。

这次一起开放的还有 Search 和 Fetch。开发者可以调用 DeepSeek 自研搜索引擎查找网页，再抓取正文，把资料交给模型处理。写代码、查文档，可以在同一个 Agent 应用里完成。

### PART.01 编程进步落在完整项目上

>>> 从终端操作到完整项目构建

与上一版 DeepSeek-V4 .1-Flash 相比，1017 的 Terminal-Bench 4.0 成绩从 31.2 升至 42.3，增加 11.1 个百分点；ProgramBench 从 20.3 升至 29.1，增加 8.8 个百分点。

软件工程测试 DeepSWE v1.1 从 74.2 升至 77.0，NL2Repo-Bench 从 65.4 升至 68.2。模型需要面对的任务包括在终端中操作环境，以及根据需求修改或构建代码仓库。

# Benchmarks
