cross_cutting.title: TypeSafe AI's Jev model speeds structured decision-making
cross_cutting.description: The launch of Jev has spurred competition, with several major tech companies releasing similar decision models. Liquid AI introduced d1, OpenAI launched its Decisions API with the Luna model, Cloudflare released Clef, AWS developed Strands Decider 2B, and Microsoft unveiled Microsoft-Decision-1.
cross_cutting.content:
# TypeSafe AI's Jev model speeds structured decision-making

TypeSafe AI introduced Jev, a decision-making AI model that aims to improve structured decision processes. The model has been designed to provide specific decision options along with confidence scores, making it faster and cheaper than traditional models. Several major tech companies have since launched competing decision models in response. Adoption of Jev was rapid, with significant usage reported shortly after its launch.

TypeSafe AI, founded by former OpenAI engineer Diogo Almeida, has introduced Jev, an AI model designed for structured decision-making. The company's valuation reached $7.5 billion weeks after the model's launch. Jev functions as a machine-learning classifier, providing specific decision options with confidence scores, rather than generating free-form language like traditional large language models (LLMs).

TypeSafe claims Jev is up to 193.6 times faster and 444.6 times cheaper than conventional LLMs for structured workflows. These include tasks such as sorting customer support tickets by department, urgency, and need for human intervention. Google Principal Architect Sathya AG noted that using an LLM for simple deterministic tasks is akin to using a smartphone solely for its flashlight.

Competitive landscape and adoption

The launch of Jev has spurred competition, with several major tech companies releasing similar decision models. Liquid AI introduced d1, OpenAI launched its Decisions API with the Luna model, Cloudflare released Clef, AWS developed Strands Decider 2B, and Microsoft unveiled Microsoft-Decision-1. These models aim to rival Jev's capabilities in text-based decisions and extend to other data types.

Vercel reported Jev's rapid adoption, reaching nearly 13 per cent of paid teams on its AI Gateway within 24 hours of launch. This made it the fastest-adopted model on the platform. Vercel's agent framework, Eve, has also made Jev its default evaluation model.

Deployment bottlenecks and validation

Despite early adoption, challenges remain for widespread enterprise deployment of decision models. Pratik Ambhore, Head of Data Engineering at RSI, highlighted evaluation as a key bottleneck. Organisations require labelled historical data, meaningful thresholds, and a clear understanding of false positive versus false negative costs.

Decision models necessitate highly specific, historical logs of past enterprise choices and exact outcomes to function accurately. A lack of this underlying factual data prevents companies from confidently predicting model behaviour. Without proper telemetry to audit and prove a model's logic, enterprises are wary of downstream system failures.

Independent evaluations also underscore the need for rigorous validation. Developer Will Kelly's experiments showed Jev's routing decisions could be influenced by misleading text, despite TypeSafe's "0 per cent hallucination rate" claim regarding schema conformity. Confidence scores provided some warning, but not a reliable safeguard against incorrect choices. Ambhore stated that decision models reduce decision-making cost and complexity, but do not eliminate validation needs.

## Comments

cross_cutting.content:
\# Jack Dorsey旗下Block推出AI语音模型Dessa，对话风格略显生疏

Jack Dorsey旗下Block发布语音AI模型Dessa，完全从人类对话数据从零训练，可在MacBook Pro M4 Max上本地运行。该模型能理解语音情绪，团队称其为真正的语音到语音模型，当前将向少数AI安全研究人员开放早期访问。

Jack Dorsey的Block公司发布了一款名为Dessa的AI模型，该模型是“完全从人类对话中从零训练而来”的。为了展示这一模型的能力，Block分享了该模型与人类进行的几段对话，其中一些对话内容显得有些生硬和诡异。

以Dessa项目负责人Ragavan Thurairatnam分享的一段对话为例，该模型与说话者之间的交流大体上保持了自然的来回互动（尽管出于某种原因，模型最初将说话者误认为是一个叫\"罗纳尔多\"的人）。

以下是一段Dessa通过语音进行猜谜游戏的视频。

Dessa官方网站还展示了其他几个示例对话，比如关于克里斯托弗·诺兰电影作品的交流（其中Dessa出人意料地跑题谈起了布莱恩·辛格执导的《超人》系列电影）、一位用户告诉Dessa自己即将带它去巴黎旅行的惊喜（网站描述称，Dessa\"随后以听起来含泪感激的语气作出回应\"），以及OpenAI的GPT\-Live\-1语音模型与Dessa之间的对话（在这段对话中，Dessa表现得更为自然）。你可以在这段视频中听到部分对话片段。

在官网上，Dessa团队表示该模型是\"真正的语音到语音模型，它所知道的一切都来自人类语音\"，并且可以在MacBook Pro M4 Max\"或更高配置\"的设备上本地运行。至于为什么要开发这款模型，团队给出了三个原因：\"好奇心（也就是有趣）、促进人类与AI之间更好的理解，以及安全性\"，并进一步解释道：

婴儿在从未见过书面文字的情况下就学会了说话。我们想看看一个模型是否也能做到这一点。结果证明可以，只是难度非常大。

语音是与任何智能体（无论是超级智能还是普通智能）交互最自然的方式，而如今的语音AI却浪费了这一优势。它们把人类说的话压缩成文本，无法跟上人类说话的节奏。

AI的能力和自主性在不断增强，但它对我们声音中的情感仍几乎“充耳不闻”。想象一下，一个人正身处剧痛之中，而语音AI对此毫无察觉，仍在滔滔不绝。这就是安全问题所在。Dessa正是朝着解决这一问题迈出的一步。

Dessa团队表示，他们将向\"一小部分AI安全研究人员\"提供该模型的早期访问权限。

cross_cutting.content:
# Anthropic和OpenAI新模型，被曝即将上线

##### 梦瑶 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI

藏！不！住！了！

Fable 5.5和GPT-6.1 Terra，竟然已经悄悄开始部署、测试了？！

前几天还在传御三家新模型大战，转眼各家新线索就被网友扒了个底朝天，主打一个「大漏特漏」。

这边，Fable 5.5被曝已经提前进入企业客户环境，摩根大通、Meta等顶级客户赫然在列：

另一边，GPT-6.1 Terra被发现出现在了GitHub员工的Copilot配置中。

甚至有传闻称，这款模型可能就是咱Tibo义父28天Codex计划的收官之作！（大彩蛋.jpg）

连谷歌也坐不住了。

Gemini 4 Flash疑似也正在后台灰度测试，据传速度飞快，能力却直逼旗舰Argon。

甚至，还有可能和Gemini 4 Carbon一起登场？？

所以……这回……真能等到正片了吧？！

## Fable 5.5被曝提前部署，可能马上要来了

一家热闹已经够热闹了，御三家凑齐，那咱可得搬好板凳唠唠。

先说友友们最最最最关心的Fable 5.5。

目前从网上流出的消息来看，Fable 5.5已经悄悄部署到部分企业客户环境中先行一步测试了。

而且客户名单的Tiltle也挺大——摩根大通、Meta等顶级企业，赫然在列。

但不管咋说，如果消息属实，那就意味着Fable 5.5离我们确实不远了～

当然啦，这还只是Fable 5.5近期曝光的线索之一。

因为时间再往前倒几天，有开发者发现Fable 5.5已经出现在微软Azure East US 2区域的模型目录中——

甚至被标记为「GenerallyAvailable」（正式可用）。

虽然这条记录随后被移除，实际调用是否开放仍有待确认。

但从云平台的模型目录，到如今传出头部企业提前测试的消息，Fable 5.5确实越来越有要来了内味儿了：

至于大家为啥这么期待Fable 5.5，还得说回它可能带来的能力升级。

此前The Information就曾爆料，A社的新款Claude在复杂推理、理解用户潜在意图和创新解题方面迎来明显提升。

虽然当时还没确认这款新Claude究竟属于Fable还是Opus系列，但不少网友已经把票投给了Fable 5.5。

更有意思的是，网上关于Fable 5.5的实测内容，甚至比这波部署爆料来得还早，鹈鹕骑车、各种svg大漏特漏。

下一步，真就差模型发布了哈。

## GPT-6.1 Terra也藏不住了，价格可能便宜一大截

另一边，关于OpenAI新模型流出的消息也来了。

据网友最新爆料，一名GitHub员工在Copilot配置中，直接把GPT-6.1 Sol替换成了尚未发布的GPT-6.1 Terra。

而且也有网友称，Terra正在作为Sol的低价替代方案接受测试。

价格甚至可能比上一代GPT-5.6 Terra便宜一大截？？？

当然，GPT-6.1 Terra也不是第一次线索流出了。

10月16日，微软公开的Entity Framework Core（EF Core）代码仓库合并了一项更新。

结果网友扒着扒着发现，微软竟然把18份评测配置中的默认评判模型，换成了尚未官宣的gpt-6.1-terra。

而且，连具体分工都给安排得明明白白——

GPT-6.1 Sol负责编程任务，GPT-6.1 Terra负责给结果打分，其中Terra的推理强度设置为medium，评判超时时间为10分钟。

如今再叠加Codex活动收官或有新模型发布的消息，难怪大家又开始猜测GPT-6.1 Terra是不是快来了。

不过话说回来，对于OpenAI下一款模型可能是GPT-6.1 Terra这事儿，网友们似乎没那么买账……

毕竟Terra在OpenAI模型家族中，一直属于兼顾能力、速度和成本的中档选手。

不少网友觉得，Terra的能力定位多少有点不上不下，尤其对面A社还憋着个Fable 5.5。

这…真能和fable上一桌吗…

## 谷歌也憋不住了？Gemini 4新模型接连曝光

眼看A社和OpenAI的新模型接连「藏不住」，谷歌这回也坐不住了——

Gemini 4 Carbon还没正式亮相，另一款Gemini 4 Flash竟然也被网友扒出了新动静。

据爆料，有网友在Google相关模型路由中，发现了一个神秘标识：Gemini 3.8-flash-router。

这里的router，简单理解就是模型的「调度员」，负责把用户请求分配给不同模型处理。

因此，有网友猜测，Gemini 4 Flash可能已经悄悄进入后台测试阶段。

而且这回更有看头的，是Gemini 4 Flas被曝出来的能力表现——

Gemini 4 Flash可能已经面向部分用户灰度测试，而且模型速度据说相当快，能力甚至已经非常接近Gemini 4 Argon？！

要知道，Argon是Google当前Gemini 4系列的旗舰模型，主攻复杂推理、编程、Agent和专业知识工作等任务。

如果Flash真能以更快的速度，逼近Argon的智能水平，那…没准…老谷歌…

这回真能让大家花更少的钱。

等更短的时间。

让大家用上接近旗舰级的模型能力了？？

都藏不住了是吧，那就索性别藏了，各家新模型赶紧端上来吧。（笑）

# Tec-Do Launches AI Agent Navos Pro For Cross-Border Marketing

27/10/2026 12:57 PM

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 (Bernama) -- Tec-Do, an artificial intelligence (AI) marketing company, has launched Navos Pro, an AI agent designed to support cross-border e-commerce, international trade, marketing and business analysis, at its Technology Growth Conference 2026 (TGC 2026) in Guangzhou.

The company describes Navos Pro as the industry’s first Pro-Agent, built around three attributes, namely professional, proactive and profitable.

“We focus exclusively on results-driven AI for Work,” said Tec-Do Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Shuhao Li in a statement.

Navos Pro builds a private knowledge base from a brand’s website and retains business context; monitors data around the clock to identify opportunities and recommend actions; and links strategy, creative work and advertising to measurable results such as sales and return on investment (ROI).

Tec-Do said Navos Pro is supported by specialised AI models, industry knowledge, more than 70 integrations with external tools and over 100 skills, and monitors more than one billion data points daily. It uses results to refine its strategies and applies reinforcement learning to keep improving the system.

The company said it became one of the first global technology partners for ChatGPT Ads in July 2026, which it said helped brands raise ROI to 2.5 times previous levels. In August, it partnered with Tencent WorkBuddy to apply AI to international advertising.

At the conference, themed “AI is Profitable”, AI pioneer Dr Kevin Knight said in his opening keynote, “From Language to Action: The Next Leap in AI”, that AI for work was a major direction for AI applications. Other speakers came from OpenAI, Google, Alibaba, ByteDance and Tencent.

Tec-Do also launched the Pro-Agent Global Challenge, inviting entrepreneurs worldwide to submit projects in agent architecture, AI marketing, AI content gateways and computing infrastructure, with access to capital and industry resources.

-- BERNAMA

cross_cutting.content:
SecurityBrief UK - Technology news for CISOs & cybersecurity decision-makers

# Oracle launches agentic AI tools & Deep Trust architecture
Mon, 26th Oct 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Oracle has introduced new Fusion Agentic Applications and a Deep Trust AI Architecture, extending its push to embed AI across its business software portfolio.

The updates span Oracle Fusion applications in finance, human resources, supply chain, sales and service. Oracle says 25 Claw-powered agentic applications are now available, designed to analyse options, prepare actions and carry out approved work within company policies and controls.

Alongside the applications, Oracle launched Fusion Companion and Fusion Agentic Home, two new AI-based interfaces for employees. The tools are intended to let users define business goals, assign work to AI systems and monitor progress, including through supported external tools such as ChatGPT.

Oracle also outlined a security and governance framework called Deep Trust AI Architecture. It is designed to apply security, privacy and business rules across four layers of the technology stack: software platform, data, data access and application development.

Chris Leone, Executive Vice President of Applications Development at Oracle, said the changes reflect a shift in how companies use enterprise software. "The next era of enterprise AI is all about delivering software that increasingly does the work, while people define the objectives and set the policies," Leone said.

"Fusion Agentic Applications, powered by Fusion Claw, can take on highly complex business processes economically and at scale. And with new AI experiences like Fusion Companion and Fusion Agentic Home, people can describe what they want to accomplish and delegate that work to AI agents and agentic applications. These innovations change how people work with enterprise software, giving them more capacity to focus on the decisions that matter while retaining control and accountability," he said.

Application rollout

The first set of agentic applications covers a wide range of operational tasks. In finance, Oracle highlighted tools such as Ledger and Payroll Activity Workspace, which review accounting entries, reconcile information, compare pay and cost data with prior periods, and propose follow-up steps for approval.

In HR, Oracle pointed to Workforce Orchestration, which assesses hiring, redeployment and external talent options to help shape workforce plans. In supply chain, Supply Planning Allocation is aimed at scarce-material allocation decisions, while Procurement Spend is designed to identify off-contract buying and savings opportunities.

Customer-facing functions are also included. Oracle says CPQ Test-to-Production Setup & Configuration Migration helps prepare and move approved configuration changes into production, while Service Health Check and Strategic Field Demand Planning focus on service performance issues and field workforce coverage.

These applications rely on Fusion Claw, an execution runtime intended for longer-running and more complex work. Oracle says the runtime supports replanning, deterministic execution and tighter governance around autonomous actions.

Intent to action

Fusion Companion acts as an intelligent layer across Fusion Applications, using business context, enterprise data and user permissions to determine which workflows, transactions, approvals, agents and applications should be involved in a task. Oracle says it can also work with information from other enterprise systems while respecting existing permissions and controls.

Fusion Agentic Home is positioned as a personalised interface built on top of that layer. It lets staff state an objective, hand work to AI systems and track the status of that work through to completion.

The announcements suggest Oracle is trying to move AI in enterprise software beyond assistance and into execution, while keeping a human approval step for higher-stakes processes. The company describes agentic applications as a new class of outcome-based software in which users set objectives and authority, and the software coordinates work to reach the result.

Trust framework

The Deep Trust AI Architecture addresses a related issue: how companies manage risk as AI systems gain wider access to business data and processes. Oracle says the framework brings together functions from Oracle AI Database, Oracle Autonomous AI Database and Oracle APEX AI Application Generator.

At the platform level, Oracle says Autonomous AI Database can automatically apply security updates across the database engine, operating system, storage and firmware before the updates are made public. It adds that rolling patching allows those changes to be introduced while applications continue to run.

At the data layer, Oracle is promoting Deep Data Security and SQL Assertions as ways to enforce user access rules and business limits in the database itself rather than only in application code. That approach is intended to stop AI-generated applications or direct database access tools from bypassing policy controls.

For data access, Oracle says Deep Trust Data APIs limit AI systems to specific business objects rather than unrestricted SQL access. It also introduced Deep NL2SQL, which adds business and data context to natural-language database queries, alongside feedback and verification tools designed to improve the accuracy of AI-generated responses.

On application development, Oracle says APEX AI Application Generator lets AI coding systems translate natural-language requests into application definitions for Oracle APEX instead of producing large volumes of executable code. Oracle argues that this model reduces maintenance and security risks because the runtime engine, rather than generated code, enforces core protections.

Juan Loaiza, Executive Vice President of AI Database Technologies at Oracle, said trust remains a central barrier to broader AI use in business systems. "AI models can now enable amazing productivity and innovation. However, enterprises can't realize these benefits if they can't trust what AI generates. AI trust is the biggest challenge we face today," Loaiza said.

"With Oracle Deep Trust AI Architecture, we are building trust into the underlying software platform, data, data access, and application development layers. This enables organizations to put AI to work while maintaining control over the information and actions that AI agents and AI-generated applications can take," he said.

Steven Dickens, Chief Executive Officer of HyperFRAME Research, said Oracle is focusing on a foundational issue in enterprise AI adoption. "The enterprise AI race is entering a new phase, and Oracle is shifting the competitive battleground from model intelligence to architectural trust," Dickens said.

"While much of the industry is still grappling with securing AI agents and governing access to enterprise data, Oracle is addressing these challenges at the source. With Deep Data Security enforcing policies directly in the database and Deep NL2SQL bringing business context, continuous learning, and verification to AI-generated answers, Oracle is fundamentally changing the equation for enterprise AI. What sets the Deep Trust AI Architecture apart is its unified approach to embedding trust into how AI accesses, understands, and acts on enterprise data. Oracle is raising the industry bar by unifying intelligence, security, and governance at the foundation of the agentic enterprise, empowering organizations to innovate faster, scale AI with confidence, and deliver more trusted business outcomes," he said.

cross_cutting.content:

# Neubird launches governed hub for AI production agents
Tue, 27th Oct 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

NeuBird has launched the Agentic Reliability Centre, a platform designed to govern AI agents that interact with production systems. The product is now generally available.

The launch addresses a growing operational challenge for large organisations as internal agents, coding assistants and third-party tools gain access to live systems through separate credentials, incur separate model costs and operate with limited central oversight. NeuBird's approach places those tools behind a single managed layer for telemetry access, model use, approvals and audit records.

According to NeuBird, ARC gives engineers and AI agents a single metered connection to telemetry and large language models. It also records each investigation in what the company describes as a shared memory layer and requires human approval before any agent action is executed, with each approval logged in a unified audit trail.

The product also extends to external and internally built tools through Model Context Protocol support. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and homegrown agents can connect through the same controls from the outset, giving them access to the same operational context and approval process.

NeuBird's own Production Ops Agent runs on ARC. According to the company, the agent can identify root cause in under five minutes with 94% accuracy and is now available inside Jira, where engineers can assign a priority-one incident to it as they would to a colleague.

Governance focus

The launch reflects broader pressure on engineering teams to use AI tools in production environments without creating new governance gaps. Many companies now use multiple assistants and agents across software development and operations, but often lack a single view of what each tool accessed, what it changed, how much model use it generated and who approved its actions.

NeuBird said ARC is built around three functions: access, memory and service. Under that structure, agents and engineers reach telemetry and models through what it calls a single governed door; every investigation is recorded, versioned and cited; and every recommended action must be approved before execution.

The system queries telemetry in place across more than 50 integrations and more than 15 sources in parallel, while storing conclusions rather than raw telemetry, according to NeuBird. It also supports Claude, GPT, Gemini, Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI and customer-hosted models, and can be deployed in cloud, virtual private cloud, on-premise, hybrid and air-gapped environments.

Gou Rao, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of NeuBird, framed the launch as a response to weak oversight of agent use in production.

"Every enterprise we talk to is building agents that touch production, and almost none of them can tell you what those agents did last week, what they cost or who approved the changes that the agent made," said Rao.

"As we lead the industry into the age of agentic production, we're giving teams the governed center to build on: telemetry connected once, models metered once, every investigation remembered and every action policy-gated," Rao said.

Customer use

RH is among the early customers cited by NeuBird. The retailer's technology team uses the platform to support site reliability engineering work, where reducing noise from observability tools and speeding incident response are significant concerns.

NeuBird said customers using its Production Ops Agent have reported 80% fewer priority-one war rooms and more than 60% lower incident management costs. Those figures were provided by the company and were not independently verified.

Nagesh Bidhurakanthu, Chief Information Officer and SVP of Technology at RH, said the business wanted stronger direction during incident response while keeping final authority with engineers.

"The resilience of our digital platform is vital to delivering a luxury experience both in our galleries and online," said Bidhurakanthu.

"Reducing time to resolution is a top priority for our SRE team, but high observability noise makes this difficult. NeuBird gives us a single, governed platform where agents can access our full stack, investigate incidents in minutes and provide engineers with clear direction. Our team still makes the final call. We just get there faster," Bidhurakanthu said.

Tooling shift

The product arrives as software vendors and in-house engineering teams move AI systems beyond coding suggestions into operational work such as incident investigation, diagnosis and change recommendation. That shift raises practical questions for enterprises around approval workflows, record-keeping, spending control and the reliability of machine-generated analysis when systems are under strain.

NeuBird's answer is not to replace engineers but to route both human and machine investigations through a shared context. According to the company, engineer corrections are captured with author attribution and version history, and any change is reversible.

Alongside ARC, NeuBird introduced NeuBird Advisor, which it said works with customer-built agents by tracing runtime reasoning, checking diagnoses against live operational context and flagging missing evidence. It also launched NeuBird for Jira on Atlassian Forge, aimed at bringing incident investigation into the ticketing workflow while keeping customer credentials in encrypted storage and requiring human approval before fixes or hand-offs proceed.

NeuBird said every action on the platform is policy-gated and covered by a single audit trail.

# [PRNewswire] Omnichat Raises US$10M Series A Led by Openspace Capita

Press Releases 11:10 October 27, 2026

HONG KONG Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire=YONHAP/ -- Omnichat [https://www.omnichat.ai/], an AI-native marketing and customer experience platform, today announced a US$10 million Series A funding round led by Openspace Capital [https://www.openspacecapital.com/], with participation from Darwin Ventures and Acorn Pacific Ventures. The company will use the funding to scale its Agentic AI platform, deepen R&D on Omni AI Agents, and accelerate global expansion.

The round will scale Omni AI Agents, the suite of AI agents Omnichat launched in 2026, to do the core work of marketing, sales and service teams inside the chat:

- AI Marketing Agent: Builds customer segments and generates complete messaging campaigns from a single prompt.

- AI Sales Agent: Recommends products and closes orders inside the chat.

- AI Customer Service Agent: Resolves customer enquiries 24/7.

- OmniClaw: An AI business analyst that tracks customer behaviour, chat trends and store-level revenue attribution in real time.

Brands have adopted the agents quickly. OmniClaw was taken up by around 300 brands within two months of its June launch. The number of brands using the Marketing Agent tripled over the same period.

Unlike shared-inbox tools that only aggregate chats, Omnichat unifies marketing, sales and customer service on a single customer profile. Omnichat also attributes revenue back to the conversation, including purchases completed in physical stores. Its agents run across WhatsApp, LINE, Facebook Messenger, Instagram, WeChat, KakaoTalk and TikTok.

Omnichat's platform has delivered measurable results for enterprises worldwide, with clients including global brands such as Dyson, FILA, Watsons, L'OCCITANE, VF Corporation, SMCP and Mead Johnson. Having helped 5,000 clients generate over US$100 million in revenue, Omnichat is now building on this foundation with agentic AI, helping businesses grow revenue without growing headcount.

"This Series A marks an important step as we transition from conversational commerce to AI-driven commerce," said Alan Chan, Founder and CEO of Omnichat. "Traditional customer messaging tools still need heavy human intervention to drive sales. With our Omni AI Agent platform, enterprises can deploy agents that sell, market, and support customers around the clock. Partnering with Openspace Capital, Darwin Ventures, and Acorn Pacific Ventures gives us the support to scale this approach across APAC and globally."

Building on its operational footprint across Asia Pacific, Omnichat will deploy its Series A capital to scale its market presence globally.

# Sprinklr Launches 6 Marketing AI Agents in Beta

7 MINUTE READ|Customer ExperienceCustomer Experience|Oct 27, 2026

OCT 27, 2026

Six specialized agents aim to compress enterprise campaign cycles from weeks to days as Sprinklr pushes deeper into agentic marketing execution.

### The Gist

Six agents, one beta. Sprinklr opened a beta for six connected marketing AI agents that span campaign ideation through budget optimization. The company has not set a general availability date.

Productivity first. Sprinklr executives told CMSWire early customers mostly use the agents for content variations and campaign trafficking. They expect recommendation and budget features to catch on in early 2027.

AI visibility is the next test. Sprinklr pitches the agents as a way to act on how brands show up in LLM answers. Tying that visibility to business outcomes remains an open problem.

Sprinklr on Oct. 27 opened a beta for Sprinklr Marketing AI Agents, a set of six connected AI agents built to help enterprise marketing teams move from market signals to live campaigns faster.

The agents cover planning, creative, campaign execution, compliance, community engagement and budget optimization. Customers can deploy them individually or run them together across a campaign. Sprinklr says people stay in control of strategy, creative and approvals.

In an interview with CMSWire ahead of the launch, Sprinklr executives said customers are pushing for this because their teams are buried in operational work while the number of channels keeps growing.

"A lot of our customers right now, they're drowning," said Anish Chadda, who leads Sprinklr's marketing product strategy. "Honestly, that's the number one feedback we get."

## Sprinklr Pitches Speed With Guardrails

Karthik Suri, Sprinklr's chief product and corporate strategy officer, says the problem is a timing mismatch. He told CMSWire a traditional campaign cycle can run four to six weeks, while a viral moment lasts roughly six days.

"Act too fast and miss out on brand ethos, brand guidelines, then you miss the mark," Suri said. "Act too slow, you miss the moment. How do you bridge these two?"

Chadda pointed to three shifts behind the product. Brands now engage consumers across more channels, and many of those channels are two-way. Brands are moving more budget toward opportunistic moments on top of always-on campaigns. And brand teams and their agencies face that workload with fewer people.

Marketing organizations also work in separate groups for social, insights, paid media and influencer programs. Chadda said that structure slows campaigns down.

"A lot of times, what happens is that these teams are still working in silos and taking information offline and feeding it back in, which is what leads to a large part of the delay in the time to market," Chadda said.

He acknowledged Sprinklr's own products grew up around that same structure, with separate tools built for each team. The agents sit on a shared data layer that pulls in paid, owned and earned data, answer engine optimization (AEO) data, video data and offline documents such as campaign briefs and wrap-up reports.

Chadda said some customers have reorganized around this model. One European home appliances brand moved ideation and campaign design into a single central team and handed activation to local teams, he said.

Suri described the design as "human in the middle."

"We've designed this to be human in the middle," Suri said. "That said, I want to make sure that the orchestration is as autonomous and as intelligent and contextual as it gets."

He compared the setup to an orchestra with a human conductor, where the level of autonomy depends on the risk of each use case.

### Sprinklr Marketing AI Agents at a Glance

Descriptions reflect Sprinklr's Oct. 27 announcement and CMSWire's interview with company executives. Capabilities are in beta.

Agent

What Sprinklr Says It Does

---|---

Ideation Agent

Connects performance, listening, audience, competitive and web signals to suggest campaign ideas, channel mix and adjustments to already-scheduled content as conditions change.

Creative Agent

Scales approved creative through editing, variations, localization and A/B testing using brand and campaign context. Sprinklr says the focus is extending approved ideas, not replacing human creative work.

Campaign Execution Agent

Turns media briefs and plans into campaigns, audiences and creative across channels. Sprinklr says it cuts setup from as long as two weeks to 30 to 60 minutes.

Compliance Agent

Checks content against brand standards, internal policies, regulatory and channel rules, and market context, then flags exceptions for human review before launch.

Community Agent

Sorts social and forum conversations by sentiment, intent and product, then helps teams respond in the brand's voice at scale.

Budget Optimization Agent

Recommends how to split budget across channels before launch and adjusts allocations while campaigns run, based on objectives and performance.

## How Sprinklr Says Customers Use the Agents

Chadda walked CMSWire through customer examples for each agent. Sprinklr did not name the customers.

### Ideation and Creative

A media streaming client had planned the same messaging for a TV show launch across every market. Chadda said the ideation agent flagged that some of the show's material could draw negative reactions in specific markets, so the client adjusted its messaging there.

On creative, Chadda said enterprise customers are cautious about fully AI-generated content and mostly use the agent for iteration.

"A lot of our enterprise customers, I don't think are completely ready for AI-based content to be rolled out," Chadda said. "But where they see a large use of AI is to help them really iterate and learn."

### Compliance

Chadda said a Big Four consulting firm told Sprinklr in September that it had published 90,000 pieces of content on LinkedIn in the first nine months of the year. The firm found about 15 versions of its logo in use. Chadda said a bigger problem was that different markets were discussing the same topics in conflicting ways. The compliance agent now checks for brand consistency and flags contradictory messaging.

In another case, the agent flagged a retail apparel client's sports-themed content, scheduled weeks earlier, after a surge of social conversation around topics in the post, Chadda said. The client could revise it before publishing.

### Campaign Execution

Chadda called campaign building one of the biggest operational burdens for brands and agencies.

"We have some customers telling us it takes them almost two weeks to build out a campaign today across all the various different channels that you have to be on," he said.

He said the campaign execution agent brings that down to 30 to 60 minutes, depending on campaign size, and has seen the heaviest adoption so far, including from agencies that have traditionally resisted new technology.

### Community

Many Sprinklr customers run community management or social care teams numbering in the hundreds, Chadda said. He distinguished the community agent from support automation.

"This is very different to a customer support use case where it's a ticketing-based system," Chadda said. "This is more thinking about how do you respond back to an individual as if you're actually having a conversation, without sounding too transactional."

## Beta, Not General Availability

Sprinklr built the agents with a group of definition partners and is now opening the beta to a broader customer set. A Sprinklr spokesperson stressed that the announcement covers the beta only, not general availability.

Chadda said productivity use cases such as content variations and campaign trafficking have taken off first. He described a top-down push inside customer organizations to adopt AI without a clear starting point.

"It's almost like a mandate, like we've got to use AI, but they don't know where to start in many cases," Chadda said.

Sprinklr is pairing the rollout with forward-deployed staff who help customers pick starting use cases and build the case for wider adoption, he said. Customers further along are moving toward the recommendation and budget optimization features.

"I anticipate the recommendation and intelligence part really kicking off, maybe in the early part of next year," Chadda said.

## The AI Visibility Question

CMSWire asked how brands can tell whether they are winning in AI-generated answers, the way SEO teams once tracked rankings. Chadda said the focus is shifting from tracking presence to acting on it.

"For the last maybe 12 to 18 months, a lot of the focus was around just monitoring and making sure, how am I showing up, where am I showing up," Chadda said. "You're now not focusing on driving consumers to your website. You're now focusing on actually designing marketing campaigns that can improve your AI visibility."

He described a large financial institution whose premium travel card is regularly compared with a competitor's. When the bank checked how its card appeared in ChatGPT and Gemini, it found the prompts centered on points redemption, and many of the LLM citations came from a handful of subreddits.

The bank made Reddit a priority, Chadda said. The ideation agent identified which conversations to monitor and which to join. The creative agent helped shape community-style responses, since overtly sponsored posts tend to get removed by Reddit moderators.

Chadda said the next step is attribution: connecting AI visibility to specific campaign objectives.

Suri said the marketing agents work alongside Sprinklr's video intelligence and LLM listening tools.

## Naver Signs AI Infrastructure Deal with Brookfield… Meets Precondition for NVIDIA Investment

Brookfield to Invest Up to $9 Billion to Secure GPU Infrastructure Naver Cloud Launches AI Factory… Alleviating the Burden of Initial Investment NVIDIA Accelerates Completion of Procedures for $1 Billion Equity Investment Naver Also Decides on Payment Guarantees Totaling 18.74 Trillion Won

[E-Daily Reporter Lee So-Hyun ] Naver (NAVER(035420)) has signed a $9 billion agreement with global alternative investment firm Brookfield to secure artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure. With this, the conditions precedent for NVIDIA’s $1 billion strategic equity investment have been met, and the 1-gigawatt (GW) global AI factory project—jointly pursued by Naver, NVIDIA, and Brookfield—has entered the full-scale implementation phase.

On the 27th, Naver announced in an amended disclosure regarding its “Future Business and Management Plans” that it had finalized a computing infrastructure agreement with Brookfield. Previously, Brookfield had been designated as the exclusive preferred negotiating party for 12 weeks to discuss a formal contract; however, this agreement has now established a concrete investment and operational structure.

Under the agreement, Brookfield will establish a special purpose vehicle (SPV) called “Asset Co. (tentative name)” and invest up to $9 billion to secure AI infrastructure, including graphics processing units (GPUs) and data centers. Naver Cloud will procure GPU-based computing resources from Asset Co. as a service (GPUaaS) to provide AI data center services to external customers.

Naver will lead the AI Factory business based on its capabilities in building and operating its own GPU clusters and its expertise in data center operations. NVIDIA plans to enhance infrastructure operational efficiency and competitiveness by providing technical cooperation centered on “DSX,” its next-generation high-performance computing platform.

Naver expects this partnership to alleviate the initial investment burden associated with building large-scale AI infrastructure. Brookfield will provide funding to secure the infrastructure, and Naver Cloud will pay usage fees tied to business revenue. Through this arrangement, the company aims to manage the financial burden during the early stages of the business while gradually expanding the infrastructure to meet AI computing demand.

Although a Brookfield-affiliated special purpose vehicle holds 100% of the equity in Asset, Naver’s control is recognized under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), and Asset is scheduled to be consolidated as a subsidiary.

This agreement is also expected to accelerate NVIDIA’s strategic equity investment in Naver. NVIDIA has agreed to participate in Naver’s third-party private placement, valued at approximately $1 billion. Since the investment’s preconditions have been met through this agreement, Naver plans to finalize the private placement process promptly and will provide further details at a later date.

AI Factory will begin operations in the first half of 2027 with a capacity of 55 megawatts (MW), using the hyperscale data center “Gak Sejong” as its core hub. It plans to increase capacity to 100 MW by the end of that year and to 200 MW by 2028. Long-term goals include building 1 GW-class infrastructure and expanding operations beyond the Asia-Pacific region into overseas markets such as Europe and the Middle East.

Meanwhile, Naver announced in a separate disclosure that day that it had decided to provide a debt guarantee worth 18.74 trillion won regarding Naver Cloud’s obligations to pay fees related to the AI Factory. This amount represents 64.73% of Naver’s equity.

This amount represents the total nominal value of GPU service fees expected to be paid through the end of 2034—the maximum contract term—assuming the full $9 billion investment limit is utilized. As of the date of the disclosure, there is no confirmed obligation to pay these fees, and the actual payment amount may vary depending on the GPU investment schedule, interest rates, and exchange rates.

Naver explained that this payment guarantee is a measure to build trust for the smooth execution of the contract, and that the guarantee itself does not immediately result in actual cash outflows or cost burdens.

# SWI Group launches SWI Compute for NVIDIA AI factories

SWI Group, a transatlantic investment firm, has launched SWI Compute to build and operate NVIDIA AI factories across Europe. This initiative includes an approximately US$1 billion order for NVIDIA hardware, with the first UK factory set for 2027.

## Highlights

- SWI Group launched SWI Compute to build and operate NVIDIA AI factories in Europe.
- The initial UK AI factory will start at 30 MW and expand to 530 MW by 2027.
- SWI Compute placed a US$1 billion order for NVIDIA GPUs and CPUs for its factories.
- The company plans 2.3 GW of NVIDIA AI factory capacity across Europe by 2029.

SWI Group, a transatlantic investment group listed on Euronext Amsterdam, has launched SWI Compute, a new AI and infrastructure provider. SWI Compute will build and operate NVIDIA AI factories, initially in Europe.Its first large-scale AI factory will be located in the UK. This site will start at 30 MW and is planned to expand to 530 MW.The UK campus is the first phase towards 2.3 GW of NVIDIA AI factory capacity by 2029. The site is expected to come online by the end of 2027.

SWI Compute has secured approximately US$1 billion in advanced NVIDIA hardware orders. These orders include close to 7,000 Rubin GPUs and 3,500 Vera CPUs.

Halil Mirakhmedov, SWI Compute Chief Executive Officer, stated the market continues to surpass available capacity. He added that the company is rapidly expanding its footprint to fulfil this requirement.

SWI Compute became a Preferred NVIDIA Cloud Partner in August. It has also finalised contracts with its first customers.SWI Group has invested in land, power, and shell since 2020. The group now holds 3.6 GW of power capacity across 24 sites in Europe and the US.Its five European campuses are located in Ireland, Denmark, Spain, Italy, and the UK. One facility has been leased to a major hyperscaler.

Max-Hervé George, SWI Group founder and Chief Executive Officer, said SWI Compute provides fully integrated infrastructure for NVIDIA AI factories. He noted SWI Group is now a transatlantic, vertically integrated digital infrastructure company.SWI Compute sites will be built to NVIDIA reference architectures. The company will design, build, and operate AI factories with the full-stack NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform.

Every new site from 2027, starting with the UK campus, will follow the NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory reference design.Nico Caprez, NVIDIA Vice President of Global AI Infrastructure Growth, stated SWI Compute is putting Europe’s energy to work for the AI ecosystem. He added that SWI Compute is building productive, durable, and fungible infrastructure.

The European data center market saw investments of US$59.84 billion in 2025. It is projected to witness investments of US$148.82 billion by 2031, according to Arizton Advisory & Intelligence.In 2025, the UK attracted the largest share of data center investment at 27 per cent. Germany followed at 12 per cent.

$9 billion deal signed… NVIDIA investment preconditions met Brookfield Capital, NVIDIA Technology, and Naver to Combine Operations CoreWeave Diversifies Financial Burden Amid Concerns Over AI Overinvestment Naver Provides 18.74 Trillion Won in Payment Guarantees… Through 2034

[Edaily Reporter Lee So-Hyun ] Naver (NAVER(035420)) has signed a $9 billion agreement with global alternative investment firm Brookfield to secure artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure. With the conditions precedent for NVIDIA’s $1 billion strategic equity investment now met, the process for NVIDIA to become Naver’s third-largest shareholder has also come into focus.

Amid growing concerns over the financial burden of large-scale investments in the global AI infrastructure market, Naver plans to enter the market by leveraging a three-party consortium model that shares capital, technology, and operations.

On the 27th, Naver announced in a revised disclosure regarding its “Future Business and Management Plans” that it had signed an agreement with Brookfield to secure computing infrastructure. This marks the finalization of the formal agreement approximately three months after Naver selected Brookfield as the exclusive preferred negotiating partner last July.

This agreement also fulfills the precondition for NVIDIA’s equity investment in Naver. NVIDIA plans to participate in a third-party private placement offering by Naver worth approximately $1 billion. If the investment is completed as scheduled, NVIDIA will become Naver’s third-largest shareholder, following the National Pension Service and BlackRock. The original payment deadline is the 30th, and Naver plans to finalize the private placement procedures as soon as possible.
Brookfield Capital, NVIDIA Technology, Naver Operations… Three-Party Alliance Gets Underway

The business structure involves Brookfield raising capital, NVIDIA providing technology, and Naver leading operations. Brookfield will establish an asset-holding company, “Asset Co. (tentative name),” through a special purpose vehicle (SPV) and invest up to $9 billion to secure AI infrastructure, including graphics processing units (GPUs) and data centers.

Naver Cloud will receive GPU-based computing resources from Asset Co. as a service (GPUaaS) to provide AI data center services to external customers. Naver will leverage its experience in building and operating its own GPU clusters and its data center operational expertise, while NVIDIA will provide technical collaboration centered on “DSX,” a next-generation high-performance computing platform.

Naver emphasizes that this partnership allows it to enter the AI infrastructure business while reducing the initial investment burden. Brookfield will provide the substantial capital required to build data centers and purchase GPUs, and Naver Cloud will pay usage fees tied to business revenue. GPU investments will also be made in phases to align with customer demand.

Concerns Over
Overinvestment Sparked by CoreWeave… Naver Emphasizes Diversifying Financial Burden

This approach is drawing attention amid concerns over financial burdens in the global AI infrastructure industry. Recently, the financing risks faced by neo-cloud companies—which rely on large-scale capital expenditures and borrowing—have come to the fore, as evidenced by the yield on corporate bonds issued by U.S. AI cloud firm CoreWeave briefly surging to 15%.

Naver’s strategy is to leverage Brookfield’s capital-raising capabilities to spread the burden of direct capital expenditures. Brookfield manages over $1 trillion in assets worldwide and has extensive experience in large-scale infrastructure investments, such as establishing a semiconductor factory joint venture with Intel and collaborating with Microsoft on energy development.

In a report released on the 19th, Shinhan Investment Securities also assessed that Naver’s AI Factory business model involves leveraging external capital to share the burden of capital expenditures, thereby allowing the company to focus on acquiring customers and monetizing operations.

The fact that Naver has a stable cash flow base from its existing businesses—such as search, advertising, and commerce—is also cited as a key differentiator from NeoCloud companies, whose revenue is heavily concentrated on GPU rentals. The plan is to secure AI infrastructure as a new growth engine while maintaining the revenue base of its existing platform businesses.
200 MW to be built by 2028… 18.74 trillion won in payment guaranteesalsosecured

Naver plans to build an AI factory with a capacity of 55 megawatts (MW) in the first half of 2027, reaching a cumulative 100 MW by the end of that year and a cumulative 200 MW by 2028, with the hyperscale data center “Gak Sejong” serving as its first hub. The long-term goal is to expand to a 1-gigawatt (GW) scale and extend the business beyond the Asia-Pacific region to overseas markets such as Europe and the Middle East.

However, this business structure also entails financial liabilities. In a separate disclosure issued today, Naver announced that it has decided to provide a debt guarantee of 18.74 trillion won for Naver Cloud’s payment obligations related to the AI Factory. This amount represents 64.73% of Naver’s equity.

This represents the total nominal amount of GPU service payments expected to be made by the end of 2034, assuming the full $9 billion investment limit is utilized. Currently, there are no confirmed payment obligations, and the actual amount may vary depending on the GPU investment schedule, interest rates, and exchange rates. The asset, which is 100% owned by Brookfield, is also expected to be consolidated as a subsidiary under Naver’s control in accordance with accounting standards.

A Naver spokesperson stated, “By combining the AI technology and data center operational capabilities we have accumulated over the years with NVIDIA’s cutting-edge computing platform capabilities and Brookfield’s global infrastructure investment capabilities, we have been able to secure both business stability and competitiveness,” adding, “Based on a capital-efficient business structure, we will create new growth opportunities in the global AI infrastructure market.”

# NAVER Signs $9 Billion AI Infrastructure Deal With Brookfield

Deal Meets Precondition for Nvidia's Strategic Equity Investment NAVER to Guarantee NAVER Cloud's Usage Fee Obligations for Up to Eight Years

Technology||

By Noh Hyun-seophit8129@sedaily.com

NAVER (035420.KS) said in a regulatory filing on the 27th that it has signed an agreement with global asset manager Brookfield to secure artificial intelligence computing infrastructure worth $9 billion, or 12 trillion won.

The deal also satisfies the precondition for a $1 billion strategic equity investment from Nvidia. NAVER plans to bring 55 megawatts online in the first half of 2027 and expand capacity to 200 megawatts by 2028.

Under the agreement, Brookfield will establish a separate special purpose vehicle, tentatively named Asset Co., to invest up to $9 billion in graphics processing units, data centers and related assets. Brookfield will supply the computing resources from that infrastructure to NAVER Cloud, which will pay usage fees linked to its business revenue. NAVER agreed to guarantee the usage fee obligations of its subsidiary NAVER Cloud for up to eight years.

The agreement reduces uncertainty over funding for the large-scale infrastructure buildout and is expected to accelerate the project.

"Through this agreement, we will secure financial stability and business scalability, and respond to surging AI computing demand at home and abroad to grow into a global leader in AI infrastructure," a NAVER official said.

# Open Innovation AI partners with VivoPower to take UAE sovereign AI expertise

Open Innovation AI has signed a head of agreement with VivoPower PLC to jointly develop secure sovereign AI data centres across the GCC, the Nordics, mainland Europe and selected markets in Asia, in a partnership that takes AI expertise built in the UAE to governments and enterprises in new markets.

The agreement was signed on Wednesday, 21 October, at Zayed National Museum in Abu Dhabi. Open Innovation AI will provide the orchestration, AI operations and security layer that lets governments run AI under their own control, and VivoPower will lead site development, power procurement and facility operations. The partners will target at least 1GW of sovereign AI capacity over the next three years, against an opportunity they estimate at more than 40GW in Europe alone.

As a first step, Open Innovation AI’s platform will be deployed across VivoPower’s existing portfolio and Nordic pipeline, which includes its site at Mo i Rana in northern Norway, with individual projects to follow under separate, project-specific agreements.

Taking UAE sovereign AI expertise to new markets

The partnership builds on the sovereign AI platforms Open Innovation AI has designed, deployed, and operated for government and enterprise environments in the UAE, one of the world’s earliest and most ambitious adopters of sovereign cloud.

In the GCC, the partners will build on Open Innovation AI’s home base in the UAE and VivoPower’s presence in Abu Dhabi to support national AI strategies across the Gulf. In Europe, many governments that want AI infrastructure under local law still depend on foreign hyperscalers for the software layer that runs it. Open Innovation AI’s AI Fabric addresses that gap with a single stack for orchestration, AI operations, agentic workflows and AI security, which runs in private cloud, on-premises and air-gapped environments without tying customers to any hardware vendor or hyperscaler.

Dr. Abed Benaichouche, Co-Founder and CEO of Open Innovation AI, said: “Sovereign AI is not only about compute capacity; it is about securing and controlling the technology layer that allows governments and enterprises to run AI safely, locally and at scale. VivoPower shares our belief that every nation should control its own intelligence. Together, we can bring secure AI Data Centres online faster across the Nordics, Mainland Europe, the GCC and Asia, and take the UAE’s AI expertise to new markets.”

Alex Cuppage, Chief Investment Officer of VivoPower PLC, said: “VivoPower is committed to being the most trusted long-term AI infrastructure partner to nations, and we believe sovereigns who build leading AI infrastructure on a secure, full-stack sovereign cloud will drive national prosperity and security. We are delighted to partner with Open Innovation AI, a proven sovereign AI orchestration and security platform that gives governments and enterprises a complete path from site to secure AI service. The UAE is globally seen as one of the most advanced nations utilising sovereign compute, and signing this agreement in Abu Dhabi, at the heart of the region’s AI ambition, is a fitting start.”

The agreement marks an important step in Open Innovation AI’s international expansion and is aligned with the direction of the UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031 and the country’s ambition to extend its AI expertise to partners abroad.
